Ruf des Chaos (Call to Chaos) in TFT Set 18

Ruf des Chaos (englisch „Call to Chaos“) ist ein Glücks-Augment für Stage 4: Du bekommst eine von 9 mächtigen Belohnungen, jede mit etwa 11 %. Die Spanne reicht von viel Gold über Erfahrung und Rerolls bis zu Ambossen, Glückstruhen und einem goldenen Ei.

Alle Belohnungen

  • Gold – 58 Gold
  • Erfahrung – 64 Erfahrung
  • Shop-Rerolls – 40 kostenlose Rerolls
  • Gegenstandsschmiede + goldenes Ei – Gegenstandsschmiede + goldenes Ei
  • Glücks-Lichtgegenstand-Truhe – 8 Gold + Glücks-Lichtgegenstand-Truhe + Gegenstandsentferner
  • Komponentenschmieden + Pfanne + Pfannenwender – 2× Komponentenschmiede + Bratpfanne + Pfannenwender
  • Diebeshandschuhe – 3× Handschuhe des Diebs + Gegenstandsentferner
  • Glückstruhen – 3× Glücksgegenstandstruhe + Gegenstandsentferner
  • verschiedene Komponenten – 6 Komponenten

Wann du es nimmst

Jede Belohnung ist für sich stark, aber sie passen zu unterschiedlichen Plänen: Gold und Erfahrung helfen jedem Board, Rerolls vor allem Reroll-Comps, Ambosse und Truhen deinem Carry. Nimm Ruf des Chaos, wenn dein Board flexibel genug ist, um aus jeder Belohnung etwas zu machen.

Wie oft du Ruf des Chaos angeboten bekommst

Ruf des Chaos ist ein Prismatisch-Augment für 4-2. Angeboten werden kann es nur, wenn diese Augment-Runde Prismatisch ist – das ist in 26,6 % der Partien so. Selbst dann ist es nur eines von vielen Prismatisch-Augments. Wie wahrscheinlich die Stufen in deiner Partie sind, zeigen die Augment-Chancen.

Häufige Fragen

Was kann Ruf des Chaos geben?

Gold, Erfahrung, Shop-Rerolls, Gegenstandsschmiede + goldenes Ei, Glücks-Lichtgegenstand-Truhe, Komponentenschmieden + Pfanne + Pfannenwender, Diebeshandschuhe, Glückstruhen und verschiedene Komponenten.

Wie wahrscheinlich ist jede Belohnung?

Alle 9 Belohnungen sind gleich wahrscheinlich, jeweils etwa 11 %.

Das goldene Ei (The Golden Egg) in TFT Set 18

Das goldene Ei (englisch „The Golden Egg“, Stage 4) gibt dir ein goldenes Ei, das nach 11 Runden schlüpft. Jeder Sieg gegen einen Spieler lässt es eine Runde schneller schlüpfen. Darin steckt reichlich Beute – von viel Gold mit Taktikerkrone bis zu fertigen Items und Lichtgegenständen.

Was im Ei stecken kann

  • 15 %: 88 Gold + Krone des Taktikers
  • 15 %: 30 Gold + 2× Krone des Taktikers + Handschuhe des Diebs
  • 10 %: 10 Gold + Krone des Taktikers + Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Zufälliges Artefakt + zufälliges fertiges Item + Gegenstandsentferner
  • 10 %: 25 Gold + Stärke der Unendlichkeit + Zhonyas Paradoxon + Der Unbeugsame + Champion-Duplikator + 2× Gegenstandsentferner
  • 15 %: 10 Gold + Krone des Taktikers + 2× Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand
  • 15 %: 25 Gold + Krone des Taktikers + Lichtversion von Handschuhe des Diebs + Handschuhe des Diebs
  • 10 %: 30 Gold + Krone des Taktikers + 4× 5-Koster + 2× Champion-Duplikator
  • 10 %: 10 Gold + Krone des Taktikers + Klinge der Unendlichkeit + Juwelenbesetzter Handschuh + Stürmerflegel + Hand der Gerechtigkeit + Quecksilber + Gegenstandsentferner

So spielst du das goldene Ei

Ohne Siege schlüpft das Ei erst nach 11 Runden – das ist lang. Mit einer Siegesserie kommt es deutlich früher. Plane dein Board so, dass du die Runden bis zum Schlüpfen überstehst: Die Beute ist groß, nützt aber nur, wenn du dann noch genug Leben hast.

Wie oft du Das goldene Ei angeboten bekommst

Das goldene Ei ist ein Prismatisch-Augment für 4-2. Angeboten werden kann es nur, wenn diese Augment-Runde Prismatisch ist – das ist in 26,6 % der Partien so. Selbst dann ist es nur eines von vielen Prismatisch-Augments. Wie wahrscheinlich die Stufen in deiner Partie sind, zeigen die Augment-Chancen.

Häufige Fragen

Was ist im goldenen Ei?

Eine von mehreren Belohnungen, die häufigsten mit je 15 % – zum Beispiel 88 Gold und eine Taktikerkrone. Alle Möglichkeiten stehen in der Tabelle.

Wann schlüpft das goldene Ei?

Nach 11 Runden. Jeder Sieg gegen einen Spieler verkürzt das um eine Runde.

Verfehlte Verbindung (Missed Connections) in TFT Set 18

Verfehlte Verbindung (englisch „Missed Connections“, ab Stage 3) gibt dir eine Kopie von jedem 1-Kosten-Champion. Im Spiel erscheinen sie als Kugeln im Kreis auf dem Spielfeld. Das Cheatsheet zeigt, welche 14 Champions dabei sind und wo sie liegen.

Alle Champions

Akali, Camille, Varus, Veigar, Ornn, Yorick, Xayah, Karma, Pebbles, Rek'Sai, Rakan, Leona, Kobuko und Cinderling.

So nutzt du es

14 Champions auf einmal sind vor allem für 1-Kosten-Reroll-Comps stark: Du bekommst Kopien deiner Carrys gratis und kommst schneller auf 3 Sterne. Auch für Attribute, die viele 1-Koster haben, füllt es dein Board. Champions, die du nicht brauchst, verkaufst du wieder für Gold.

Wie oft du Verfehlte Verbindung angeboten bekommst

Verfehlte Verbindung ist ein Silber-Augment für 3-2 und 4-2. Angeboten werden kann es nur, wenn eine dieser Augment-Runden Silber ist – das ist in 37,6 % der Partien so. Selbst dann ist es nur eines von vielen Silber-Augments. Wie wahrscheinlich die Stufen in deiner Partie sind, zeigen die Augment-Chancen.

Häufige Fragen

Welche Champions gibt es bei Verfehlte Verbindung?

Akali, Camille, Varus, Veigar, Ornn, Yorick, Xayah, Karma, Pebbles, Rek'Sai, Rakan, Leona, Kobuko und Cinderling.

Was gibt Verfehlte Verbindung?

Eine Kopie von jedem 1-Kosten-Champion des Sets.

Ein Teil des Lebens (Slice of Life) in TFT Set 18

Ein Teil des Lebens (englisch „Slice of Life“, Stage 2) gibt dir zweimal pro Stage einen zufälligen Champion, der mit jeder Stage teurer wird. Der Effekt endet, nachdem du einen 5-Kosten-Champion bekommen hast.

Wann es welchen Champion gibt

  • 2-1: ein zufälliger 2-Koster
  • 2-5: ein zufälliger 2-Koster
  • 3-1: ein zufälliger 3-Koster
  • 3-5: ein zufälliger 3-Koster
  • 4-1: ein zufälliger 4-Koster
  • 4-5: ein zufälliger 4-Koster
  • 5-1: ein zufälliger 5-Koster

Zusammen sind das 7 Champions im Wert von 23 Gold.

So nutzt du es

Die Champions sind zufällig, aber jeder ist Gold wert: Passt einer, ist es eine Gratis-Kopie für dein Board. Passt keiner, verkaufst du ihn und hast trotzdem Gold gewonnen. Am meisten bringt das Augment, wenn du es früh nimmst und lange im Spiel bleibst.

Wie oft du Ein Teil des Lebens angeboten bekommst

Ein Teil des Lebens ist ein Silber-Augment für 2-1. Angeboten werden kann es nur, wenn diese Augment-Runde Silber ist – das ist in 25,7 % der Partien so. Selbst dann ist es nur eines von vielen Silber-Augments. Wie wahrscheinlich die Stufen in deiner Partie sind, zeigen die Augment-Chancen.

Häufige Fragen

Wie viele Champions gibt Ein Teil des Lebens?

7 Champions bis Runde 5-1.

Wann endet Ein Teil des Lebens?

Nachdem du einen 5-Kosten-Champion bekommen hast.

Bindende Verpflichtung (Hard Commit) in TFT Set 18

Bindende Verpflichtung (englisch „Hard Commit“, Stage 2) bindet dich an ein Attribut: Du bekommst ein zufälliges Emblem. Sofort und zu Beginn jeder Stage gibt es dazu einen 1-Stern-Champion mit diesem Attribut, dessen Kosten zur Stage passen (höchstens 5), und 3 Gold.

Die möglichen Attribute

7 Attribute kommen in Frage: Blossom, Brawler, Elderwood, Hunter, Juggernaut, Spellweaver und Vanguard. Die Tabelle zeigt zu jedem Attribut die Champions ab 2 Kosten, die du bekommen kannst.

So spielst du es

Der Name sagt es: Du legst dich fest. Das Augment lohnt sich, wenn du das Attribut bis zum Ende spielst – dann bekommst du jede Stage einen passenden Champion und Gold dazu. Wechselst du später die Comp, verliert es den größten Teil seines Werts.

Wie oft du Bindende Verpflichtung angeboten bekommst

Bindende Verpflichtung ist ein Prismatisch-Augment für 2-1. Angeboten werden kann es nur, wenn diese Augment-Runde Prismatisch ist – das ist in 9,2 % der Partien so. Selbst dann ist es nur eines von vielen Prismatisch-Augments. Wie wahrscheinlich die Stufen in deiner Partie sind, zeigen die Augment-Chancen.

Häufige Fragen

Welche Attribute gibt es bei Bindende Verpflichtung?

Blossom, Brawler, Elderwood, Hunter, Juggernaut, Spellweaver und Vanguard.

Was gibt Bindende Verpflichtung jede Stage?

Einen 1-Stern-Champion mit deinem Attribut, dessen Kosten zur Stage passen, und 3 Gold.

Solo-Stufenaufstieg (Solo Leveling) in TFT Set 18

Solo-Stufenaufstieg (englisch „Solo Leveling“, Stage 2) setzt alles auf einen Champion: Für die nächsten 5 Kämpfe darfst du nur eine Unit aufs Feld stellen. Dafür bekommt sie starke Zusatzwerte, und du erhältst für jeden Kill 1 XP. Danach gibt es 2 Komponenten.

Die Zusatzwerte

  • 50 % Angriffsschaden
  • 50 % Fähigkeitsstärke
  • 150 % Angriffstempo
  • 10 % Krit-Chance
  • 30 % Schadensverstärkung
  • 525 Leben
  • 20 % Haltbarkeit
  • 20 % Omnivampir

So spielst du es

5 Kämpfe mit nur einer Unit bedeuten meist ein paar Niederlagen – rechne mit Lebensverlust. Wähle einen Champion, der allein lange überlebt und Schaden macht, und gib ihm deine besten Items. Jeder Kill bringt XP, und nach den 5 Kämpfen hast du 2 Komponenten mehr für dein richtiges Board.

Wie oft du Solo-Stufenaufstieg angeboten bekommst

Solo-Stufenaufstieg ist ein Gold-Augment für 2-1. Angeboten werden kann es nur, wenn diese Augment-Runde Gold ist – das ist in 65,1 % der Partien so. Selbst dann ist es nur eines von vielen Gold-Augments. Wie wahrscheinlich die Stufen in deiner Partie sind, zeigen die Augment-Chancen.

Häufige Fragen

Welche Werte gibt Solo-Stufenaufstieg?

50 % Angriffsschaden, 50 % Fähigkeitsstärke, 150 % Angriffstempo, 10 % Krit-Chance, 30 % Schadensverstärkung, 525 Leben, 20 % Haltbarkeit und 20 % Omnivampir.

Wie lange dauert Solo-Stufenaufstieg?

5 Kämpfe. Danach ist dein Team wieder normal groß, und du bekommst 2 Komponenten.

Prismatische Attribute (Prismatic traits) in TFT Set 18

Mit genug Champions eines Attributs auf dem Feld wird es prismatisch und bekommt stärkere Effekte als die normale höchste Stufe. In Set 18 geht das bei Blossom und Elderwood. Das Cheatsheet zeigt die Bedingungen und was sich jeweils ändert.

Blossom prismatisch

11 Blossom-Champions aufs Feld (mindestens 2 Embleme nötig). Geister laden sich mit Kraft auf und werden zu ihren prismatischen Effekten.

Elderwood prismatisch

11 Elderwood-Champions aufs Feld (mindestens 2 Embleme nötig). Pflanzen steigen auf 3 Sterne auf, und alle 7 Sekunden erscheinen Tiefwald-Beschützer.

So erreichst du die prismatische Stufe

Für 11 Champions eines Attributs reicht dein Board allein meist nicht – du brauchst mindestens zwei Embleme. Pfannenwender und Bratpfanne sind deshalb der Schlüssel. Woher du sie bekommst und welches Emblem aus welchem Rezept entsteht, steht im Cheatsheet zu den Emblemen.

Häufige Fragen

Wie wird Blossom prismatisch?

11 Blossom-Champions aufs Feld (mindestens 2 Embleme nötig). Geister laden sich mit Kraft auf und werden zu ihren prismatischen Effekten.

Wie wird Elderwood prismatisch?

11 Elderwood-Champions aufs Feld (mindestens 2 Embleme nötig). Pflanzen steigen auf 3 Sterne auf, und alle 7 Sekunden erscheinen Tiefwald-Beschützer.

Coven-Beute in TFT Set 18

Coven sammelt Essenz, wenn deine Champions Gegner töten – und noch mehr, wenn du eine PvP-Runde verlierst. Ab 40 Essenz entscheidest du: jetzt in Beute umwandeln oder weitersammeln. Jede Stufe braucht mehr Essenz und gibt bessere Beute, bis 800 Essenz. Das Cheatsheet zeigt jede Stufe mit allen möglichen Belohnungen.

Essenz pro Stufe

Coven-Championspro Killpro Niederlage
3222
4228
5335
71060

Mit mehr Coven-Champions sammelst du deutlich schneller – vor allem durch Niederlagen.

Die Beute-Stufen

  • 40 Essenz: 3 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 4 Gold
  • 85 Essenz: 3 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 2 Gold + 1 Komponente
  • 130 Essenz: 3 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 1 Komponente + 3× Caitlyn oder 3× Elise
  • 185 Essenz: 4 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel Gegenstandsschmiede + 1 Komponente
  • 250 Essenz: 5 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 20 Gold + Gegenstandsschmiede + Gegenstandsschmiede
  • 365 Essenz: 6 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 27 Gold + Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + 2× Gegenstandsentferner + 2× Umgestalter
  • 500 Essenz: 5 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 3× Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Gegenstandsschmiede + Gegenstandsschmiede + 3× Gegenstandsentferner + 3× Umgestalter
  • 650 Essenz: 3 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 30 Gold + 3× 5-Koster + 3× 5-Koster + 3× 5-Koster + Schild des Taktikers + Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Goldener Gegenstandsentferner
  • 800 Essenz: 2 mögliche Belohnungen, zum Beispiel 100 Gold + 3× Umhang des Taktikers + 6× Zufälliger Lichtgegenstand + Goldener Gegenstandsentferner

Umwandeln oder weitersammeln?

Wer früh umwandelt, bekommt sofort Beute für ein stärkeres Board. Wer weitersammelt, riskiert Leben – vor allem, wenn Niederlagen die meiste Essenz bringen –, kann aber eine der großen Stufen erreichen. Behalte dein Leben im Blick: Eine große Belohnung nützt nur, wenn du sie noch einsetzen kannst.

Häufige Fragen

Wie viel Essenz bekommt Coven pro Kill?

(3) 2 pro Kill und 22 pro Niederlage, (4) 2 pro Kill und 28 pro Niederlage, (5) 3 pro Kill und 35 pro Niederlage und (7) 10 pro Kill und 60 pro Niederlage.

Wie viel Essenz brauchst du für die beste Coven-Beute?

800 Essenz.

Riftbeast-Shop & Buffs in TFT Set 18

Mit 5 Riftbeasts ist jeder dritte Shop voller Riftbeasts. Diese Shops nutzen feste Aufstellungen statt der normalen Shop Odds – das Cheatsheet zeigt pro Level, wie wahrscheinlich mindestens eine Kopie jedes Riftbeasts ist. Dazu kommen die Buffs, die eine Riftbeast mit dem Alpha-Mal bekommt.

Der Riftbeast-Shop

Ab 5 Riftbeasts ist nach jedem dritten Kampf dein nächster Shop voller Riftbeasts. Welche kommen, hängt von deinem Level ab. Auf Level 8 sind Krug (76 %), Mama Beak (52 %) und Gromp (51 %) am häufigsten. Den Elder Dragon gibt es erst ab Level 9 (5 %), auf Level 10 mit 45 %.

Die Chancen gelten für Level 4 bis 10 und zählen mindestens eine Kopie im Shop. 3-Sterne-Riftbeasts sind dabei nicht berücksichtigt.

Die Buffs mit dem Alpha-Mal

(3) Mit dem Alpha-Mal erhält eine Riftbeast ihren eigenen Buff.

  • Cinderling – Scharlachroter Buff: Erhält bei jedem Zauber 22 % Angriffsschaden.
  • Pebbles – Petrol-Buff: Erhält 2 Manaregeneration pro 4 Sekunden Kanalisieren.
  • Gromp – Lila Buff: Erhält alle 5 Sekunden 30 % Fähigkeitsstärke.
  • Murkwolf – Grauer Buff: Erhält Präzision und 25 % Krit-Chance, bis zu 75 % je nach fehlendem Leben.
  • Scuttlecrab – Grüner Buff: Fallen Verbündete unter 50 % Leben, stellen sie 15 % ihres maximalen Lebens wieder her.
  • Mama Beak – Oranger Buff: Normaler Schaden senkt die Rüstung des Gegners um 2.
  • Krug – Schiefer-Buff: Beim Tod schützen Krug und Kruglets Verbündete mit einem Schild über 8 % des maximalen Lebens.
  • Brambleback – Roter Buff: Angriffe verbrennen Gegner um 1 % und heilen Brambleback um 5 % des maximalen Lebens.
  • Sentinel – Blauer Buff: Bei jedem Zauber erhalten Verbündete 2 Manaregeneration.
  • Elder Dragon – Buff des Ältesten Drachen: Schaden an Gegnern unter 12 % Leben richtet sie hin.

Häufige Fragen

Wie oft kommt ein Riftbeast-Shop?

Mit 5 Riftbeasts nach jedem dritten Kampf.

Ab welchem Level gibt es den Elder Dragon im Riftbeast-Shop?

Ab Level 9 (5 %), auf Level 10 mit 45 %.

Blackthorn-Boni in TFT Set 18

Bei Blackthorn wird der Verbündete auf dem Blackthorn-Feld vor dem Kampf geopfert. Alle deine Champions bekommen dafür Leben, Blackthorn-Champions zusätzlich Werte je nach Rolle, Sternen und Kosten des Opfers. Das Cheatsheet zeigt alle Werte für Tanks, AD- und AP-Champions.

Was die Rolle des Opfers gibt

  • Tank: 17 % maximales Leben und 12 Rüstung und Magieresistenz (Grundwert)
  • AD-Champion: 24 % Angriffsschaden und 14 % Angriffstempo
  • AP-Champion: 10 % Schadensverstärkung und 2 Manaregeneration

Diese Grundwerte werden mit den Kosten und Sternen des Opfers multipliziert – ein teures Opfer mit vielen Sternen gibt ein Vielfaches.

Die Blackthorn-Stufen

Blackthorn ist mit 2, 4 und 6 Champions aktiv. Auf jeder höheren Stufe gibt es mehr Leben für alle, und die Boni für deine Blackthorn-Champions werden stärker.

Wen du opferst

Leg einen Champion aufs Feld, den du ohnehin nicht im Kampf brauchst – zum Beispiel eine Kopie, die du später sowieso verkaufst. Die Rolle bestimmt, welche Werte deine Blackthorn-Champions bekommen: Brauchen sie mehr Haltbarkeit, opfere einen Tank, brauchen sie mehr Schaden, einen AD- oder AP-Champion. Welche Rolle ein Champion hat, zeigt der Kampf-Simulator.

Häufige Fragen

Welchen Champion solltest du opfern?

Je teurer und je mehr Sterne, desto höher die Boni. Die Rolle des Opfers bestimmt die Werte: Tanks geben Leben und Resistenzen, AD-Champions Angriffsschaden und Angriffstempo, AP-Champions Schadensverstärkung und Manaregeneration.

Bekommen alle Champions etwas vom Opfer?

Alle Champions bekommen Leben. Die zusätzlichen Werte je nach Rolle bekommen nur Blackthorn-Champions.

Fae-Pixies & Gold in TFT Set 18

Schaden, Heilung und Schilde deines Teams locken Pixies an. Jede Pixie gibt Fae-Champions Angriffsschaden und Fähigkeitsstärke und heilt sie, wenn sie unter 50 % Leben fallen. Nach 7 Pixies kommen stattdessen goldene Pixies, die Gold geben. Das Cheatsheet zeigt alle Schwellen und Werte.

Wann Pixies kommen

Die erste Pixie kommt ab 2.000 Schaden, Heilung und Schilden, die 7. ab 155.000. Die Werte summieren sich über die Partie – je stärker dein Board kämpft, desto schneller füllt sich die Leiste.

Goldene Pixies

  • ab 170.000: 5 Gold
  • ab 200.000: 8 Gold
  • ab 300.000: 12 Gold
  • ab 400.000: 18 Gold
  • ab 500.000: 25 Gold
  • ab 600.000: 50 Gold
  • ab 888.888: 777 Gold

Die letzte Schwelle bei 888.888 gibt sogar 777 Gold – sie erreichst du nur in sehr langen Partien.

Das Augment Vergrößern

Pixies werden größer und geben 50 % mehr AD und AP. Fae-Champions erhalten sofort 18 % AD und AP.

Häufige Fragen

Wie viel Gold geben goldene Pixies?

Von 5 Gold ab 170.000 bis 777 Gold ab 888.888.

Was macht das Augment Vergrößern?

Pixies werden größer und geben 50 % mehr AD und AP. Fae-Champions erhalten sofort 18 % AD und AP.

Primal-Segen in TFT Set 18

Primal lässt dich einen von 4 Segen wählen: Schildkröte, Bär, Tiger und Phönix. Jeder Segen verstärkt dein Team auf eine andere Art – von Heilung über Hinrichtungen bis zu Angriffstempo und Komponenten. Das Cheatsheet zeigt, was jeder Segen bewirkt.

Die Segen im Überblick

  • Schildkröte: Dein Team heilt alle 4 Sekunden 4 % seines maximalen Lebens.
  • Bär: Primal-Schaden richtet Gegner unter 12 % Leben hin.
  • Tiger: Nach 6 Sekunden erhalten Primal-Champions 35 % Angriffstempo und dein Team 15 % Angriffstempo.
  • Phönix: Alle 15 Primal-Kills erhältst du eine Komponente (höchstens 4).

Welchen Segen du wählst

Primal ist mit 2 und 4 Champions aktiv. Welcher Segen am besten ist, hängt von deinem Board ab: Die Heilung hilft Boards, die lange Kämpfe führen, die Hinrichtung Boards mit viel Primal-Schaden, das Angriffstempo Teams mit Auto-Angriff-Carrys. Der Komponenten-Segen lohnt sich, wenn du früh viele Kills sammelst und noch Items brauchst.

Was macht der Segen Tiger?

Nach 6 Sekunden erhalten Primal-Champions 35 % Angriffstempo und dein Team 15 % Angriffstempo.

Was macht der Segen Phönix?

Alle 15 Primal-Kills erhältst du eine Komponente (höchstens 4).

Cheatsheet
Avatar

Lux bekommt je nach gewähltem Attribut einen Zusatzeffekt.

L
Lux · Grundeffekt

Passiv: Bei jedem Zauber erhalten alle Verbündeten, die ein Attribut mit Lux teilen, 3/3/100 Mana.

Aktiv: Feuert einen Laser in die Linie mit den meisten Gegnern: 375/565/6500 magischer Schaden, pro getroffenem Gegner 25/25/10 % weniger (mindestens 40 %).

Blackthorn

Betäubt getroffene Ziele für 1 Sekunde.

Blossom

Coven

Elderwood

Fae

Inferno

Stellt pro Kill 8 Mana wieder her.

Lunar

Macht getroffene Gegner für 4 Sekunden 10 % verwundbar.

Primal

Nach dem Zauber 6 Sekunden lang 50 % Angriffstempo.

Solar

Avatar (Lux) in TFT Set 18

Lux bekommt als Avatar je nach gewähltem Attribut einen Zusatzeffekt auf ihre Fähigkeit. Zur Auswahl stehen 9 Attribute – Blackthorn, Blossom, Coven, Elderwood, Fae, Inferno, Lunar, Primal und Solar. Das gewählte Attribut zählt für die Trait-Stufen doppelt. Das Cheatsheet zeigt jeden Effekt und Lux' Grundfähigkeit.

Lux' Grundfähigkeit

  • Passiv: Bei jedem Zauber erhalten alle Verbündeten, die ein Attribut mit Lux teilen, 3/3/100 Mana.
  • Aktiv: Feuert einen Laser in die Linie mit den meisten Gegnern: 375/565/6500 magischer Schaden, pro getroffenem Gegner 25/25/10 % weniger (mindestens 40 %).

Die Effekte je Attribut

  • Blackthorn: Betäubt getroffene Ziele für 1 Sekunde.
  • Blossom: Das erste getroffene Ziel erleidet 10 % zusätzlichen Schaden.
  • Coven: Senkt Rüstung und Magieresistenz getroffener Ziele für den restlichen Kampf um 8.
  • Elderwood: Zauber geben allen Verbündeten für den restlichen Kampf 2,5 % mehr maximales Leben.
  • Fae: Heilt den Verbündeten mit dem niedrigsten Leben in Prozent um 18 % des Fähigkeitsschadens.
  • Inferno: Stellt pro Kill 8 Mana wieder her.
  • Lunar: Macht getroffene Gegner für 4 Sekunden 10 % verwundbar.
  • Primal: Nach dem Zauber 6 Sekunden lang 50 % Angriffstempo.
  • Solar: Verursacht 15 % zusätzlichen Schaden, plus 12 % je einzigartigem 3-Sterne-Champion auf dem Feld.

Welches Attribut du wählst

Wähle zuerst das Attribut, das dein Board ohnehin spielt: Da es doppelt zählt, erreichst du damit eine höhere Trait-Stufe. Der Zusatzeffekt auf Lux ist der Bonus obendrauf. Hast du einen Avatar auf der Bank oder dem Feld, nehmen alle weiteren Avatare im Shop dasselbe Attribut an.

Häufige Fragen

Was macht Lux als Avatar?

Aktiv: Feuert einen Laser in die Linie mit den meisten Gegnern: 375/565/6500 magischer Schaden, pro getroffenem Gegner 25/25/10 % weniger (mindestens 40 %).

Welches Attribut ist für Lux am stärksten?

Das hängt von deinem Team ab: Das Attribut, das du ohnehin spielst, gibt Lux den Effekt und zählt für deine Trait-Stufen doppelt.

TFT Sprykin BFF & SFF

TFT Sprykin BFF & SFF für Set 18: Werte und Belohnungen des Attributs. Alle Werte übersichtlich als Tabelle im TFTClimb Cheatsheet.

Sprykin BFF & SFF

Cheatsheet
Sprykin 3 / 5 / 7

Du erhältst den besten flauschigen Freund (BFF). Setze einen Sprykin darauf, um seinen Reiter zu wählen. Mit „Small Furry Friend“ (ab Stage 2) kommt ein zweiter, kleinerer Freund (SFF) mit 45 % der Stärke dazu.

BFF- und SFF-Effekte
BFF
  • (3) Reiter: 15 % · 15 %
  • (5) Reiter: 40 % · 40 % · 50 % der BFF-Fähigkeit wirkt auf deine Sprykin-Champions
  • (7) Reiter: 55 % · 55 % · 100 % der BFF-Fähigkeit wirkt auf deine Sprykin-Champions
SFF
  • (3) Reiter: 6,75 % · 6,75 %
  • (5) Reiter: 18 % · 15,75 % · 50 % der BFF-Fähigkeit wirkt auf deine Sprykin-Champions
  • (7) Reiter: 24,75 % · 24,75 % · 100 % der BFF-Fähigkeit wirkt auf deine Sprykin-Champions
BFF-Fähigkeit (Nahkampf)
BFF

Der BFF brüllt und heilt den Reiter und andere Verbündete um % ihres maximalen Lebens.

  • (3) 10 % Reiter
  • (5) 13 % Reiter, 6,5 % andere Verbündete
  • (7) 16 % Reiter, 16 % andere Verbündete
SFF

Der SFF brüllt und heilt den Reiter und andere Sprykin um % ihres maximalen Lebens.

  • (3) 4,5 % Reiter
  • (5) 0,6 % Reiter, 0,3 % andere Sprykin
  • (7) 7,2 % Reiter, 7,2 % andere Sprykin
BFF-Fähigkeit (Fernkampf)
BFF

Der BFF tanzt und gibt dem Reiter für den restlichen Kampf AD und AP.

  • (3) 15 % Reiter
  • (5) 30 % Reiter, 15 % andere Sprykin
  • (7) 40 % Reiter, 40 % andere Sprykin
SFF

Der SFF tanzt und gibt dem Reiter für den restlichen Kampf AD und AP.

  • (3) 6,75 % Reiter
  • (5) 12,6 % Reiter, 6,3 % andere Sprykin
  • (7) 15 % Reiter, 15 % andere Sprykin

Sprykin BFF & SFF in TFT Set 18

Mit Sprykin bekommst du einen besten flauschigen Freund (BFF). Setzt du einen Sprykin-Champion darauf, wird er zum Reiter. Mit dem Augment „Small Furry Friend“ kommt ab Stage 2 ein zweiter, kleinerer Freund (SFF) mit 45 % der Stärke dazu. Das Cheatsheet zeigt die Werte für Nahkampf- und Fernkampf-Reiter.

Die Sprykin-Stufen

Sprykin ist mit 3, 5 und 7 Champions aktiv. Auf jeder Stufe bekommt der Reiter mehr Leben und Angriffstempo. Ab der zweiten Stufe erhalten deine Sprykin-Champions zusätzlich einen Teil der Fähigkeit des BFF.

Nahkampf oder Fernkampf?

Welche Werte der BFF gibt, hängt davon ab, ob der Reiter im Nahkampf oder auf Distanz kämpft. Fernkampf-Reiter bekommen in der Tabelle die höheren Prozentwerte, Nahkampf-Reiter stehen dafür vorne und halten mehr aus. Setz den Champion auf den BFF, der deinem Board gerade fehlt.

Das Augment Kleiner pelziger Freund

Solange Sprykin aktiv ist, bekommst du eine zweite BFF-Beschwörung mit 45 % der Stärke, dazu einen Teemo, einen Veigar und einen Kobuko. Das lohnt sich, wenn du Sprykin bis zum Ende spielst.

Häufige Fragen

Wie stark ist der Small Furry Friend?

Er hat 45 % der Stärke des BFF.

Wie wählst du den Reiter des BFF?

Setz einen Sprykin-Champion auf den BFF – er wird dann zum Reiter.

Patch-Plan für TFT Set 18: alle Termine

Riot bringt TFT-Patches etwa alle zwei Wochen. Der Patch-Plan zeigt alle Termine von Set 18 mit den Events dazu, vom Battle Pass bis zu den Turnieren. Den aktuellen und den nächsten Patch markiert die Tabelle automatisch. Als Nächstes kommt Patch 18.6 am 4. November 2026.

Wie oft TFT gepatcht wird

In Set 18 liegen im Schnitt 14 Tage zwischen zwei Patches. Dazwischen gibt es manchmal B-Patches wie 18.6B – kleine Nachbesserungen, wenn etwas zu stark ist oder nicht funktioniert. Jeder Patch kann die Stärke von Champions, Items und Augments verändern.

Die nächsten Termine

  • Patch 18.6 – 4. November 2026: Patch für 1 Woche, 4v4 Superbrawl
  • Patch 18.6B – 11. November 2026: Worlds, Set 19 PBE
  • Patch 19.1 – 1. Dezember 2026: Set 19 startet

Wann Set 19 startet

Set 19 startet mit Patch 19.1 am 1. Dezember 2026. Schon ab Patch 18.6B (11. November 2026) kannst du es auf dem PBE ausprobieren. Bis dahin bleibt Set 18 aktiv.

Events in diesem Set

Battle Pass Teil 1, TPC Cup #1, Tactician's Trials #1, Woche 1, TPC Cup #2, Tactician's Trials #1, Woche 2, TPC Cup #3, Battle Pass Teil 2, Tactician's Trials #2, Regionals, Patch für 1 Woche, 4v4 Superbrawl, Worlds, Set 19 PBE und Set 19 startet.

Profi-TippClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Nach jedem Patch neu bewerten

Nach einem Patch können Comps, die vorher stark waren, deutlich schwächer sein – und umgekehrt. Lies die Patch Notes und schau in die Tierlist, bevor du deine Lieblings-Comp einfach weiterspielst.

Häufige Fragen

Wann kommt der nächste TFT-Patch?

Patch 18.6 ist für den 4. November 2026 geplant.

Wann startet Set 19?

Mit Patch 19.1 am 1. Dezember 2026.

Was ist ein B-Patch?

Ein kleiner Zwischen-Patch nach einem großen Patch, mit dem Riot schnell Fehler behebt oder zu starke Dinge abschwächt.

Inhalt geprüft vonClaudio „CrazYSlayt“TFT Challenger · TFTClimb Coach

Claudio spielt TFT auf Challenger-Niveau und coacht bei TFTClimb Spieler auf dem Weg nach oben.

pre.home:
TFTClimb: TFT tier list, tools and cheatsheets for Set 18

TFTClimb is the TFT site of Challenger player Claudio “CrazYSlayt”. Here you find everything for your climb in Teamfight Tactics: a tier list with the strongest comps of patch 18.5, free calculators, cheatsheets with every number of the set, a library with every champion, item and trait – and coaching if you want to climb faster.

29comps in the tier list for patch 18.5
7free TFT tools
38cheatsheets with every number of the set

The TFT tier list for patch 18.5

The tier list rates 29 comps from S to C, plus situational comps for special spots. Every comp shows its board, items, augments and game plan. Currently in S tier: Draven Dragon 9. There are also tier lists for items, augments and the champions worth holding in stage 1.

Free TFT tools

Every tool runs in your browser, without sign-up and with the data of the current patch:

  • Rolldown calculator – Will you hit your units?
  • Augment odds – How often is prismatic?
  • DPS calculator – Which item build wins?
  • Item drop odds – Which component comes next?
  • Team Builder – Plan and share your board
  • Battle simulator – Which board wins?
  • Tier list maker – Create your own tier list

Cheatsheets: every number of the set

38 cheatsheets for a quick look next to the game: shop odds and XP, augment tiers, encounters, loot orbs, player damage, emblems plus tables for single augments and traits. You can cut out every table as an image and share it.

Library and patch notes

The library holds all 65 champions, 35 traits and every item and augment of Set 18 with the official values. We prepare the patch notes after every patch – sorted by champions, traits, items and augments.

Coaching by TFTClimb

Want to improve with purpose? In coaching we look at your games and work on the decisions that cost you LP – from econ and rolldowns to positioning.

FAQ

Is TFTClimb free?

Yes. Tier list, tools, cheatsheets, library and patch notes are free and need no sign-up. Coaching is a separate offer.

How often is the tier list updated?

With every patch, so about every two weeks. New, rising and falling comps are marked in the tier list.

Is TFTClimb available in German?

Yes, every page is also available in German. You can switch the language in the settings at the top right.

/en/tier-list.d: TFT tier list Set 18 (Patch 18.5): the best comps with positioning, items, augments and game plan.

pre.tl:
TFT tier list patch 18.5: the best comps in Set 18

Our tier list rates 29 comps by their strength in patch 18.5, from S to C, plus situational comps that only work in certain spots. Every card shows carry, traits and items; a click opens board, augments and game plan. Strongest right now: Draven Dragon 9.

1comp in S tier
29comps in patch 18.5
5situational comps

How to read the tier list

  • S (Overpowered): the strongest comps of the patch – 1 comp.
  • A (Strong): very strong and often just as good if you find the units – 5 comps.
  • B (Meh): playable, but with clear weaknesses – 12 comps.
  • C (Euuuuw): only when everything lines up – 6 comps.
  • Situational (Niche): strong with the right augment, encounter or item – 5 comps.

The comp types

Use “comp type” to filter the tier list by play style:

  • Reroll (1, 2 or 3 cost): you roll on a low level until your cheap carries are 3 stars.
  • Fast 8: you save health and gold and look for your 4-cost carries on level 8.
  • Fast 9: maximum econ for the 5-costs on level 9.
  • Lose streak: lose on purpose early, collect gold and components, stabilise later.

How much gold a rolldown for your comp needs is worked out by the rolldown calculator.

When the tier list changes

After every patch we re-check the ratings. New comps and comps that rise or fall are marked. What changed in the patch is in the patch notes.

FAQ

Which comp is the best right now?

S tier currently holds Draven Dragon 9.

What does “situational” mean in the tier list?

These comps are only strong with the right augment, encounter or item. Play them when your game offers them.

How often is the tier list updated?

With every patch, so about every two weeks.

pre.tl:
TFT item tier list for patch 18.5

The item tier list shows which items are strongest in Set 18 right now – from regular combined items to radiant versions, artifacts and emblems. Click an item for its stats and recipe.

The four item types

  • Combined: items from two components – you build these almost every game.
  • Radiant: upgraded versions of regular items, for example from augments or encounters.
  • Artifacts: special items from artifact anvils with unique effects.
  • Emblems: 20 emblems that give a champion another trait.

How to use the item tier list

The rating shows an item's overall strength. Which item fits your carry best depends on its ability – compare that directly in the DPS calculator. Which components you can expect right now is shown by the item drop odds.

FAQ

Which items are the strongest in TFT?

The items at the top of the tier list. For your carry, what matters most is whether the item fits its ability.

How do I build an emblem?

From a spatula or a frying pan plus a component. Every recipe is in the emblem recipes cheatsheet.

pre.tl:
TFT augment tier list for patch 18.5

The augment tier list rates every augment of Set 18 – split into silver, gold and prismatic and by the stage you pick it on. So on 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2 you see at a glance which pick is strongest.

Why the stage matters

Many augments are stronger early than late – or the other way round. An economy augment gives much more on 2-1 than on 4-2, a combat augment gets stronger with a finished board. That is why you can filter the tier list by 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2.

Silver, gold or prismatic?

Which tier comes in your game is set at the start. How likely each sequence is, is shown by the augment odds and the Augment tiers cheatsheet.

FAQ

Which augment should I take?

The highest rated augment that fits your board and stage. When in doubt, a strong economy augment early is the safer pick.

How often is there a prismatic augment?

The augment odds show it: almost half of all games have at least one prismatic augment.

pre.tl:
TFT holds: which champions to keep in stage 1

In stage 1 you decide which champions to hold – pairs for early 2-star units or champions that fit the strongest comps. The holds tier list rates 1-, 2- and 3-costs by how worthwhile they are from 1-1 to 1-3.

Why good holds matter

Holding the right champions early gives you a stronger board in stage 2 and costs less health. Some 1-costs even win the PvE rounds on their own – which ones is in the Solo Stage 1 cheatsheet.

FAQ

What does “hold” mean in TFT?

Keeping a champion on your bench instead of selling it – usually for a pair or because it fits your planned comp.

pre.rolldown:
TFT rolldown calculator Set 18: shop odds, pool and gold needed

The rolldown often decides the whole game: do you roll down now or level first? The rolldown calculator shows how likely you are to hit your units. It uses the TFT odds of Set 18: the shop odds per level, the pool size of each cost tier and the shared pool of all eight players. Here you find all reroll odds of patch 18.5 as tables – and live in the calculator above.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“
Most important: scout!

With 50 gold you hit a 4-cost ★★ in 41% of games – if an opponent already holds 3 copies, only in 21%. For 8 out of 10 games you then need 120 Gold instead of 84 Gold. If someone plays your unit, you have three options:

  1. Roll earlier – before your opponent takes even more copies out of the pool.
  2. Roll with more gold – work out the difference in the calculator above under “Is anyone else playing this unit?”.
  3. Switch to a unit nobody plays – uncontested units are much cheaper to hit.
  • 4-cost carry? Level 8 first, then roll. For ★★ in 8 out of 10 games you need about 262 Gold at level 7, but only 84 Gold at level 8 – even with up to 56 gold for levelling you come out cheaper.
  • 1-cost reroll? Don't level too early. For ★★★ in 8 out of 10 games you need 155 Gold at level 5, 229 Gold at level 6, 431 Gold at level 7. Higher levels show fewer 1-costs.

Encounters that change your rolldown

Some encounters give you gold, rerolls or cheaper levels – then a different plan for your rolldown pays off.

How the rolldown calculator works

  • Shop by shop with the shared pool: every copy you find is then missing from the pool.
  • Every hit costs its price in gold – just like in the game. Many other calculators leave that out and end up too optimistic.
  • The free shop at the start of the round is included.
  • Other units of the same cost held by players make your unit a bit more common. Without your own input the calculator uses a guideline based on level.
  • Effects that change shops, such as augments, are not included.

How to use the rolldown calculator

  1. Pick the cost of your unit. Which champion it is doesn’t change the odds – all champions of a cost tier have the same number of copies.
  2. Pick your goal – ★★ (3 copies) or ★★★ (9 copies) – and how many copies you already have.
  3. Tell the calculator whether anyone else plays the unit. Under “Detailed” it also compares whether levelling first pays off.
  4. Pick your level and the gold you want to spend – for rolling and buying.

FAQ

What does rolldown mean in TFT?

In a rolldown you spend a lot of gold on rerolls at once to find the key units of your comp and make your board strong.

What are the 4-cost odds at level 8?

At level 8, every shop slot is a 4-cost with 30% – at level 7 only with 10%.

How many copies of each unit are there?

In Set 18: 30 per 1-cost, 25 per 2-cost, 18 per 3-cost, 10 per 4-cost, 9 per 5-cost. All eight players share this pool.

How much gold do I need for a 3-star 1-cost?

At level 5 about 121 Gold for 5 out of 10 games and 155 Gold for 8 out of 10 – if nobody else plays the unit.

How much does a reroll cost?

A reroll costs 2 gold and shows you 5 new units. The cost tiers come with the odds of your current level.

Do bought units count?

Yes. Every hit costs its price in gold, like in the game – the more you find, the less gold is left to roll.

pre.drops:
TFT item drop odds Set 18: which component comes next?

Components from the creep rounds aren’t pure luck: they come from an item pool with the 8 basic components. Whatever has dropped is missing from the pool – so the remaining components become more likely. The item drop odds keeps count for you and shows which component can come next.

8components in the item pool
≈ 12random components from stage 1 to 4-7 on average
14%chance of at least one gold orb by 4-7

How the item pool works

  • At the start the pool holds exactly one of each of the eight components.
  • Every component that drops is then missing from the pool.
  • Before every new creep stage (2-7, 3-7, 4-7) one of each component is added.
  • Frying Pan and Spatula are not part of the pool – they come from orbs, augments or encounters.

Loot per stage

StageComponents on averageAt least one gold orbAt least one prismatic orb
Stage 13.0––
2-72.45%–
3-73.54%2%
4-73.15%2%

Random components from minion and creep rounds, not counting components from orbs. What’s inside the orbs is shown in the loot orb cheatsheet.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“
No component drops twice in stage 1

Since there is only one of each component in the pool, you get each one at most once from the minion rounds. A second copy can drop at 2-7 at the earliest. So plan your first item from what you already have – not around a second copy of the same component.

Exception: item augments. If you get an augment that gives components, you can slam an item with two identical components early – the second one doesn’t come from the item pool then.

If you take several component augments, you quickly lose track of what came from the creep rounds. So only enter drops from minion and creep rounds above – components from augments aren’t part of the pool.

The more components have dropped, the more predictable the next drop becomes. After three or four entered drops you see exactly which items are realistic.

How to use the item drop odds

  1. Pick the current stage.
  2. Click every component as soon as it drops.
  3. Read which components are most likely to come next and plan your items around them.

FAQ

Are item drops in TFT random?

Not entirely. Components come from an item pool: whatever has dropped is missing from it until new components are added.

When are new components added to the pool?

Before every new creep stage, one of each component is added.

Do spatula and frying pan come from the pool too?

No. They are not part of the item pool – they come from gold orbs, augments or encounters, for example.

What drops from stage 5 on?

No more random components. Against Xerath you get orbs at 66% and 33% of his health and an anvil for a finished item when you win.

TFT tier list maker: create your own tier list for Set 18

Got your own take on the meta? With the TFT tier list maker you create your own tier list for Set 18: sort champions, items, artifacts, emblems and augments into rows by drag & drop and share the result with a link – in Discord or with your duo, for example.

What you can rank in Set 18

CategoryCountExamples
Champions65

Items36
Artifacts30
Emblems20
Augmentsall of the setsortable by tier: silver, gold, prismatic

Ideas for your tier list

  • Rate augments for 2-1 differently from 4-2 – early on tempo counts, late game strength counts.
  • Rank the best carries of one trait – for your favourite comp, for example.
  • Build a tier list made only of artifacts or emblems.
  • Stage 1 holds: one tier list each for 1-, 2- and 3-costs – which units are worth holding early?
  • Rank the same category as your duo and compare links.

How we see the meta is in our TFT tier list with comps, items, augments and holds.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“
  • Rank stage 1 holds. I also use it for our holds tier list for stage 1: filter by cost at the top and rank 1-, 2- and 3-costs separately – so you see at a glance which units are worth holding early.
  • Rate for one situation. There is no “best item” – an item can be strong on the carry and useless on the tank. Put what the list is for in the title, e.g. “Items for AD carries”.
  • Use the X row. Put everything that only works in certain comps there. That keeps S to C clean.

How to make your tier list

  1. Pick the category at the top: champions, items, artifacts, emblems or augments.
  2. Drag the tiles into the rows – or tap a tile first and then a row.
  3. Rename the rows and change colors and order. Up to 12 rows are possible.
  4. With “Share” you get a link that shows exactly your tier list.

FAQ

Is the tier list maker free?

Yes, completely free and without sign-up.

Is my tier list saved?

Yes, your draft stays in your browser automatically. To share it you create a link – whoever opens it sees exactly your tier list.

Can I change the rows?

Yes. You can rename rows, change their color and order and use up to 12 rows. The default is S, A, B, C and X.

Where do the images and names come from?

From the official game data of the current set. After a patch, new champions, items and augments are included automatically.

pre.sim:
TFT battle simulator Set 18: test your teams before you play them

Which board wins – yours or your opponent’s? In the TFT battle simulator you set up two teams with items, stars and augments and watch the fight step by step: who moves where, whom they attack, when they cast and who deals the most damage. It uses the game data of Set 18 and the same combat rules as the game.

100fights for the win chance
30 sthen overtime starts
6roles decide mana and targeting

The rules the units fight by

  • Tanks first. If several enemies are equally far away – for example on the first attack – a unit prefers to attack the tank, and assassins last. That is why it pays to place your tanks so they soak up the first attacks.
  • Target: otherwise every unit attacks the nearest enemy – the one with the fewest steps to get in range. Until it reaches its target, it re-checks after every hex.
  • After crowd control: if a unit is stunned or knocked up, it keeps its target afterwards as long as it is in range. Riot changed this with Set 18 – before, units retargeted the closest enemy after a stun.
  • Mana: depends on the champion’s role (table below). Only tanks gain mana from damage taken. No mana while casting or while stunned.
  • Damage: base damage × crit × damage amp, reduced by armor or magic resist and damage reduction.
  • Overtime: from 30 seconds, damage and attack speed rise by 10% every second, while healing, shields and crowd control get weaker.

Roles: mana and targeting

Since Set 15 every champion has one of six roles. It decides how they gain mana and how often they become the target at equal distance.

So a 3-star champion has more than three times the health of a 1-star. How stars and cost compare is shown in the hierarchy of power cheatsheet.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“
  • Test against your real opponent. Scout the board you lose to most and rebuild it as the enemy. That way you don’t test against any board, but against the one costing you health right now.
  • Two positionings, 100 fights each. Put your carry in the corner once and somewhere else once, and calculate the win chance each time – small position changes often matter more than an item.

What the simulator can’t do

  • Riot doesn’t provide exact numbers for every ability – where they are missing, strength is estimated by cost and mana cost.
  • Very special effects of some traits or augments may be simplified.
  • The results are guidelines: ideal for comparing two variants, not for predicting the exact outcome.

Battle simulator or DPS calculator?

The simulator lets two whole teams fight – with movement, targeting and enemies hitting back. If you only want to know which item build deals the most damage on one carry, the DPS calculator is quicker: it compares up to four builds of the same champion.

How to use the battle simulator

  1. Set up your team and the enemy team – or load comps straight from the tier list.
  2. Start the fight and skip forward or back.
  3. Click a unit to see its target, path, stats and next action.
  4. Run the fight 100 times to see both teams’ win chance.

FAQ

How accurate is the battle simulator?

It follows the known combat rules of TFT: targeting, movement, mana and overtime. Some ability strengths are estimated, so results are guidelines – good for comparing positioning and item spreads.

How does it calculate the win chance?

With “Win chance” the simulator runs the same fight 100 times with different randomness, e.g. crits, and counts how often each team wins.

Can I load comps from the tier list?

Yes. You load comps from our tier list straight into the simulator and adjust them there.

How long does a fight last?

Overtime starts at 30 seconds. If there is no winner after 45 seconds, the fight ends in a draw.

pre.dps:
TFT DPS calculator Set 18: which item build deals the most damage?

Which item build deals the most damage? The TFT DPS calculator lets your champion fight enemies that don’t hit back and shows in a graph how the damage of up to four builds builds up. In Set 18 you can test 43 carries and damage units – with items, emblems, traits and shred and sunder from your team.

4item builds compared at once
24fights per build – the average smooths out crits
43champions in Set 18 to test

What goes into the calculation

  • Attacks: attack damage (AD) × attack speed, plus crit chance and crit damage.
  • Ability: how often the champion casts depends on mana – by role 7 (casters, plus 2 per second) or 10 per attack (fighters, marksmen, assassins), plus mana from items. Its strength scales with ability power (AP) or AD.
  • Damage amp: items like Deathblade or Giant Slayer increase every hit by a percentage.
  • Enemies: the targets’ armor and magic resist reduce the damage – more on that below.

The key damage items in Set 18

ItemADAPAttack speedKritDamage ampRamps up
Infinity Edge35 %––35 %–
Deathblade55 %–––10 %
Giant Slayer15 %1515 %–15 %
Last Whisper15 %–20 %20 %–
Guinsoo's Rageblade–1010 %––✓
Kraken's Fury10 %–10 %––✓
Red Buff––45 %–6 %
Rabadon's Deathcap–55––15 %
Jeweled Gauntlet–35–35 %–
Blue Buff15 %15–––
Archangel's Staff–30–––✓
Hextech Gunblade20 %20–––

Values from the set’s game data. “Ramps up”: the item grows with attacks or over time – such items tend to win long fights. Which items our carries use is shown in the item tier list.

Armor, magic resist, shred and sunder

Armor reduces physical damage, magic resist (MR) reduces magic damage. The enemy takes 100 / (100 + armor) of the damage. Sunder lowers armor by 30%, shred lowers MR by 30% – the tankier the target, the more it helps.

Enemy in the calculatorHealthArmor / MRDamage dealtwith sunder/shred
Backline8003077 %83 %
Frontline16007059 %67 %
Tank300015040 %49 %

Shred and sunder don’t stack – if another unit on your board already applies sunder, your own Last Whisper adds nothing for that.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“
  • Compare at the right second. Items that ramp up win long fights, instant items win short ones. Look at your builds at 10 and at 25 seconds – if the winner changes, your board decides: if your carry dies fast, take the build that leads early.
  • No double sunder or shred. If another unit on your board already applies sunder or shred, switch it on above – the effect doesn’t stack. Often a build without Last Whisper or Void Staff wins then.
  • Test against the right enemy. Your carry wins most fights by getting through the frontline. So test against “Frontline” or “Tank”, not just “Backline”.

Total damage or damage per second?

“Total damage” shows the summed-up damage – so you see which build leads at the deciding second. “Damage per second” shows how hard a build hits right now: items like Guinsoo’s Rageblade or Kraken’s Fury climb over time, items like Deathblade work from the first second.

How to use the DPS calculator

  1. Pick a champion and its stars. Tanks are left out on purpose – they are not built for damage.
  2. Put together up to four item builds, emblems included. The builds from our tier list are pre-filled.
  3. If another unit on your board already applies shred or sunder, switch it on.
  4. Under “Detailed” you set trait tiers and the enemies – backline, frontline or tank and how many stand next to each other.
  5. Set the second you want to compare up to and read the damage in the table.

FAQ

How accurate is the DPS calculator?

It uses the engine of our battle simulator: base stats and items come from Riot, ability strength is estimated where Riot provides no numbers. That works well for comparing builds; the absolute numbers are guidelines.

Do traits and emblems count?

Yes. Under “Detailed” you set the active tier for each of the champion’s traits. Emblems in a build add their trait. Augments are not included.

Why is the result an average?

Crits are random. That is why the DPS calculator runs every build 24 times and shows the average.

What is the difference between shred and sunder?

Sunder lowers the enemy’s armor, shred lowers their magic resist – each by 30%. So sunder helps physical damage and shred helps magic damage.

Why are some champions missing?

Tanks are not built for damage – the DPS calculator only lists carries and damage units.

pre.augments:
TFT augment odds in Set 18: how likely is a prismatic augment?

Every TFT game gives you three augments – on 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2. Whether they are silver, gold or prismatic is not rolled round by round: the tiers of the whole game are set as one combination. In Set 18, 48% of all games have at least one prismatic augment. Here you find all augment tier odds of patch 18.5 – including your prismatic augment chance on 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2 – as tables and live in the calculator above.

48%at least one prismatic augment per game
9%prismatic already on 2-1
20%most common game: Gold – Gold – Gold

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

If you know your next augment will be gold, you can turn that into an advantage:

  • Augmented Power makes your next augment one tier higher – gold turns into prismatic.
  • Advanced Loan gives you gold right away, but your next augment is one tier lower. Gold turns into silver – but you don’t miss out on a prismatic.

This is safest with Golden Gala (7% of games): every augment is gold there – so from 2-1 on you know every next augment will be gold and can plan your picks around it right away.

That gives you an edge over your opponents. How sure your next augment is gold is shown by the calculator above: after Gold on 2-1 and Silver on 3-2, 4-2 is gold in 90% of games, for example.

››

Encounters that change your augments

Some encounters fix the augment tiers at the start of the game – the normal distribution above doesn't apply to those augments. With “Golden Gala”, for example, every augment is gold. So you know for sure which tier comes next and can plan your augment picks around it – just like in the pro tip above.

Augments with items

Many augments give components or finished items – such as “Nesting Anvils” or “Component Buffet”. Which component comes next from the creep rounds is shown by our item drop odds.

How augment tiers work

  • The tiers of all three augments are fixed as one combination at the start of the game – for example gold, gold, prismatic.
  • In every augment round all players get augments of the same tier.
  • Rerolling changes the offered augments, not their tier.
  • The odds apply to Set 18 and can change with patches – we update them with every patch.

You can see every order with its odds as a tree in the augment cheatsheet.

How to use the augment calculator

  1. Under “Your input”, pick the tier of your augment on 2-1.
  2. Under “Your result”, read which tier is likely on 3-2 and how high your odds of a prismatic augment still are.
  3. On 3-2, enter the next tier – the odds for 4-2 get more precise.

FAQ

What is the chance of a prismatic augment in TFT?

In Set 18, 48% of all games have at least one prismatic augment. The odds are 9% on 2-1, 18% on 3-2 and 27% on 4-2.

Can I get two or three prismatic augments?

Yes, but rarely: 6% of games have at least two prismatic augments, three in 1%.

Do all players get the same augment tier?

Yes. In every augment round all players get augments of the same tier – only the choices differ.

Can I influence the tier of my augments?

No. The tiers of all three augments are set as one combination at the start of the game. Rerolling changes the offered augments, not their tier.

Where do the numbers come from?

From the augment distribution of Set 18 (Little Buddy Bot · Patch 18.5). We update it with every patch – the same values are in the augment tree of our cheatsheet.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“
  • Plan two boards, not one. Build your transition board for level 6 to 7 and your goal board for level 8 – and save both as a link. In game you then know which units to buy early and replace later.
  • Items on the carry first. On the right the builder shows which components your items need. Check with the item drop odds which of them can still drop in your game.
  • Test your positioning. Use “Enemy” to set up the board of your strongest opponent and let both fight in the battle simulator .

What the team builder does

  • Place units by drag & drop or by tapping – on mobile too.
  • Up to three items per unit, including emblems, artifacts and radiant items.
  • See active traits and their tier, pick augments and read off the components you need.
  • Set up an enemy board next to yours and hand both to the battle simulator.
  • Share teams as a link or team code – in Discord or for coaching, for example.

How to use the team builder

  1. Drag units onto the board – or tap a unit first and then a hex.
  2. Give your units items and click the stars to change their star level.
  3. On the left you see all active traits, on the right augments and the components your items need.
  4. Share your team as a link or team code. With “Enemy” you also set up an enemy board.

FAQ

Is the TFT team builder free?

Yes, free and without sign-up. Your board stays saved in your browser.

How many units fit on my board?

As many as your level: at level 8 you field 8 units. So plan your traits for the level you want to play at.

How many traits are there in Set 18?

35 – 23 origins and 12 classes. 10 of them belong to a single champion.

How do I share my team?

With the icons at the top right: copy link or copy team code. Use “Import” to load a code or link again.

Can I build teams from earlier sets?

Yes. Use the set selector to switch to older sets or to the PBE preview when it is available.

TFT patch notes: every change of Set 18

Here you find every TFT patch note neatly prepared: each change to champions, traits, items and augments, sorted and searchable. The current patch is 18.5, next up is patch 18.6.

When new patches arrive

Riot ships a new TFT patch about every two weeks. In between there are sometimes small B-patches that adjust single values. When exactly the next patch drops is shown by the patch countdown, every date of the set is in the Patch schedule cheatsheet.

How we prepare the patch notes

  • Every change sorted by champions, traits, items and augments – with icons instead of long text blocks.
  • A search across all changes of a patch, for example for your favourite champion.
  • If Riot publishes the German version later, you see the English one until then – it gets replaced automatically.

Every patch in the archive

The archive holds 14 patches from Sets 18 and 17. So you can look up when a champion or item got stronger or weaker – handy when a comp suddenly moves in the tier list.

FAQ

When is the next TFT patch?

Next up is patch 18.6. The patch countdown shows the exact time.

What is a B-patch?

A small follow-up patch after a main patch that Riot uses to quickly fix bugs or tone down things that are too strong.

Where do the patch notes come from?

From the official patch notes by Riot Games. We sort and prepare them – if in doubt, the original at Riot applies.

The TFT cheatsheet for every game

Many decisions in TFT depend on fixed numbers: when is level 8 worth it for 4-cost units? How likely is another prismatic augment? What's inside a gold orb? Here are all system values of Set 18 on one page – for a quick look next to the game.

FAQ

What are the odds of a prismatic augment?

The first augment is prismatic in about 9% of games. Almost half of all games (about 48%) have at least one prismatic augment.

How much damage do I take after a loss?

The stage damage plus 1 for every enemy unit that survives the fight.

How do I build an emblem?

Spatula or Frying Pan plus a component. Which emblem you get is listed in the emblem recipes table.

TFT shop odds in Set 18: odds per level, XP and pool

Shop odds decide how likely each of the five shop slots shows a champion of a given cost – the higher your level, the more expensive the champions. On level 8 a 4-cost shows up with 30% per slot, on level 9 a 5-cost with 15%. The cheatsheet also lists how many copies of each champion exist and how much XP you need for the next level. Here we explain how to read the numbers and what they mean for your roll-or-level decision.

30%4-costs per shop slot at level 8
200XP from level 1 to level 9
10copies of every 4-cost in the pool

How to read the shop odds

For each of the five slots the game first rolls the cost tier – with the odds of your level – and then draws a champion of that tier from the shared pool. On level 8 that means per slot: 15% 1-cost, 20% 2-cost, 32% 3-cost, 30% 4-cost and 3% 5-cost. On average you see 1.5 4-costs per shop there.

The odds apply to the cost tier, not to one specific champion. How often your unit shows up also depends on how many copies of it and of the other champions of that tier are left in the pool. That is exactly what the rolldown calculator works out for you.

Level 7, 8 or 9: what changes

Level3-cost4-cost5-cost4-costs per shop
625%5%0%0.25
743%10%1%0.5
832%30%3%1.5
925%33%15%1.65
1020%40%25%2

The biggest jump happens from level 7 to 8: the odds for 4-costs rise from 10 to 30% – that is 3 times as much. From level 8 to 9 the 4-costs only gain 3 percentage points, but 5-costs go from 3 to 15%. So level 9 pays off mainly when you are looking for 5-costs – level 10 even brings 25%.

XP and gold: what a level costs

You get 2 free XP every round, and 4 gold buys 4 XP. The table shows how much XP each level needs and what it costs in gold if you buy all of it – the free XP from rounds lowers the price.

LevelXPGold (all bought)

9 → 106868

From level 1 to level 9 you need 200 XP in total. The most expensive steps are 7 → 8 (56 XP) and 8 → 9 (68 XP). That is why the timing of level 8 is one of the most important decisions of the game.

CostCopies per championChampionsCopies in total

All eight players draw from the same pool. A 4-cost at ★★ needs 3 of its 10 copies, ★★★ even 9. If an opponent already holds copies, it gets much harder – so check the other boards before every rolldown.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Level first, then roll

If you play a 4-cost carry, roll on level 8: there you see 1.5 4-costs per shop on average instead of 0.5 on level 7 – every 2-gold reroll is worth much more. For 1- and 2-cost reroll comps the opposite is true: stay on a level where your cost tier still shows up often and roll there.

FAQ

Which level do you roll on for 4-cost champions?

Usually on level 8: 4-costs show up with 30% per shop slot there, on level 7 with only 10%. Level 9 has 33%, but 15% 5-costs already mix in.

How much XP do you need for level 9?

Level 8 to 9 takes 68 XP, level 1 to level 9 takes 200 XP in total.

How much gold does level 9 cost?

Level 8 to 9 takes 68 XP. Buying all of it costs 68 gold – the 2 free XP per round lower the price.

How many copies of a champion are there?

30 for 1-costs, 25 for 2-costs, 18 for 3-costs, 10 for 4-costs and 9 for 5-costs – shared by all players.

Hierarchy of power in TFT Set 18: stars vs. cost

The hierarchy of power ranks every combination of cost and star level by its strength in combat. It answers a question from almost every game: is it worth swapping a 2-star champion for a more expensive 1-star one? The short answer: one more star roughly makes up for two cost tiers. Here you learn how the chart works, which rules of thumb follow from it and when you should not swap.

How to read the chart

The chart has three columns – 3 stars, 2 stars and 1 star. Each column holds the five cost tiers. The higher a unit sits, the stronger it is. A ≈ between two units means: about equally strong. As a list from strong to weak:

  1. ★★★ 5-cost
  2. ★★★ 4-cost
  3. ★★★ 3-cost ≈ ★★ 5-cost
  4. ★★★ 2-cost
  5. ★★ 4-cost
  6. ★★★ 1-cost
  7. ★★ 3-cost ≈ ★ 5-cost
  8. ★ 4-cost
  9. ★★ 2-cost
  10. ★★ 1-cost
  11. ★ 3-cost
  12. ★ 2-cost
  13. ★ 1-cost

The key rules of thumb

  • ★★★ 3-cost ≈ ★★ 5-cost – equally strong, items and traits decide.
  • ★★ 3-cost ≈ ★ 5-cost – equally strong, items and traits decide.
  • ★ 4-cost beats ★★ 2-cost – an expensive champion on one star is already stronger than a cheap one on two.
  • ★★★ 1-cost sits between ★★ 4-cost and ★★ 3-cost – a 3-star 1-cost is a real carry for the midgame.

When to swap a champion

The chart only tells you which unit is stronger in combat. Whether a swap pays off also depends on your board:

  • Traits: if the new champion breaks an active trait breakpoint, you often lose more than you gain.
  • Role: swap frontline for frontline and carry for carry. A stronger champion in the wrong role does little for your board.
  • Items: when you sell a champion, its items go back to your bench. Check whether they fit the new champion.

Where the rule of thumb does not fit

The hierarchy of power is a rule of thumb by CrazYSlayt, not an exact calculation. Reroll carries are built to get much stronger at 3 stars than their cost suggests. Some 5-costs have abilities that swing a fight even at one star. And every patch moves single champions up or down – when in doubt, the tier list shows who is strong right now.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Don't sell too early

If you only find a fitting 5-cost at 1 star, it is about as strong as your ★★ 3-cost. Keep the champion that activates your traits and only swap once you can bring the 5-cost to 2 stars – then it is clearly ahead.

FAQ

Is a 3-star 3-cost stronger than a 2-star 5-cost?

They are about equally strong. Items and the traits the champion activates in your team decide which one is better.

Is a 1-star 4-cost stronger than a 2-star 2-cost?

Yes, according to the hierarchy of power the 1-star 4-cost is slightly ahead.

When should you swap a champion for a more expensive one?

When the new champion ranks at least as high in the chart, has the same role and does not break your traits. If it ranks lower, keep the higher star level.

Content checked byClaudio „CrazYSlayt“TFT Challenger · TFTClimb Coach

Encounters in TFT Set 18: every chance and effect

Encounters change the game before the first round: sometimes you start with anvils, sometimes with extra gold, prismatic augments or special champions. Set 18 has 19 different encounters, plus games without any encounter (3.4%). There is exactly one per game. Here you find every encounter sorted by type, with its odds and effect.

19different encounters
6.8%for the most common ones
3.4%games without an encounter

Types of encounters

TypeCountCombined odds
Item encounters419.3%
Augment encounters731.8%
Champion encounters426.1%
Economy encounters312.5%
Other16.8%

The odds apply per game. Within a type the encounters differ in frequency – the exact values are in the sections below.

Item encounters

You start with anvils or emblems – good for early items and a strong start.

  • Completed Item Anvil (6.8%): You start with a completed item anvil.
  • Component Anvils (6.8%): You start with 2 component anvils.
  • Item Forge (3.4%): All players start with 2 completed item anvils.
  • Emblem Ensemble (2.3%): You start with 3 random emblems.

Augment encounters

They lock augment tiers or give you more choice.

  • Golden Gala (6.8%): All augments offered are gold.
  • Golden Prelude (4.5%): The first augment is gold.
  • Golden Finale (4.5%): The last augment is gold.
  • Prismatic Prelude (4.5%): The first augment is prismatic.
  • Prismatic Finale (4.5%): The last augment is prismatic.
  • Scouting Party (4.5%): You get +1 augment reroll.
  • Prismatic Party (2.3%): All augments offered are prismatic.

Champion encounters

You start with extra or better champions.

  • 2 Cost Start (6.8%): You start with a random 2-cost champion.
  • Upgraded Start (6.8%): Your starting champion is already ★★.
  • Howling Abyss (6.8%): You start with 5 random 1-cost champions.
  • 3 Cost Start (5.7%): You start with a random 3-cost champion.

Economy encounters

More gold, free rerolls or cheaper levels.

  • Cheaper Levels (4.5%): Every level costs 2 less XP.
  • Gold Subscription (4.5%): At the start of every stage, all players get the same amount of gold.
  • Reroll Subscription (3.4%): At the start of every stage you get free shop rerolls.

Other

Everything that fits no other group.

  • Final Showdown (6.8%): The final two players get 70 gold for the last fight.
Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Plan around the encounter right away

The encounter is set before the first round. If it gives you items or a strong starting champion, play for an early win streak. Economy encounters like Gold Subscription reward clean interest and a planned rolldown. And if an encounter locks the augment tier, you know before 2-1 what to expect.

FAQ

Which encounter is the most common?

The most common ones are Completed Item Anvil, Component Anvils, Golden Gala, 2 Cost Start, Upgraded Start, Howling Abyss and Final Showdown with 6.8% each.

How often is there no encounter?

3.4% of games have no encounter.

How many encounters are there per game?

Exactly one. It is rolled at the start of the game and lasts until the end.

Player damage in TFT Set 18: how much health a loss costs

When you lose a fight against a player you take damage: the fixed stage damage plus 1 for every enemy unit that survives. Stage damage rises from 2 in stage 2 to 17 in stage 7. Use the cheatsheet to judge how long you can afford a lose streak and when every loss becomes dangerous.

2stage damage in stage 2
10stage damage in stage 5
150from stage 8 – every loss ends the game

How damage is calculated

Damage = stage damage + 1 per surviving enemy unit. How strong the surviving units are or what they cost does not matter – only their number counts.

StageStage damagewith 3 units leftwith 6 units left
2258
36912
471013
5101316
6121518
7172023

How much of a lose streak you can afford

A stage usually has five fights against players. If you lose all of them in stage 2 and stage 3 and three enemy units survive each time, that costs 25 + 45 = 70 health. Of your 100 health, 30 remain. An early lose streak is doable – but you need to stabilise in stage 4, where every loss already costs 10 or more.

What a whole stage of losses costs

Say you lose every fight from stage 2 on and three enemy units survive each time. This is how fast your 100 health melts:

Stageper loss5 losseshealth after
252575
394530
41050out

In practice almost everyone wins some fights along the way – the table just shows how much room a deliberate lose streak has.

Late stages

From stage 5 on damage climbs fast: 10 in stage 5, 12 in stage 6 and 17 in stage 7 – plus the surviving units. A loss in stage 6 against a full board with 6 surviving units costs 18 health. From stage 8 stage damage is 150, so every loss ends the game.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Health is a resource

Health is a resource in TFT, just like gold: in stages 2 and 3 you can spend it on a strong economy as long as you have a plan to stabilise before stage 4. If you reach stage 5 with low health, you have to spend your gold on your board instead of interest.

FAQ

How much damage do you take in stage 4?

7 damage plus 1 for every surviving enemy unit – so 12 if five units survive.

Does the cost of the surviving units matter?

No, only their number: every surviving enemy unit adds 1 damage.

Why does stage 8 show 150 damage?

From stage 8 on, stage damage is so high that every loss ends the game.

Loot orbs in TFT Set 18: what is inside each orb?

Loot orbs drop in PvE rounds and from some augments. Each colour holds something different: gray orbs are worth about 2–3 gold, blue ones 6–8 gold, gold ones 14–18 gold and prismatic ones around 40 gold. The cheatsheet lists every possible content per colour with its odds. Here you learn when each orb drops and why the stage changes what is inside.

≈ 40gold in a prismatic orb
≈ 18gold in a gold orb from stage 4
≈ 2gold in a gray orb

The colours at a glance

OrbStageValueMost common content
Gray orbStage 1–2≈ 2 Gold2 random 1-costs (48%)
Gray orbfrom stage 3≈ 3 Goldrandom 3-cost (49%)
Blue orbStage 1–3≈ 6 Gold2 random 3-costs (33%)
Blue orbfrom stage 4≈ 8 Gold4 Gold + random 4-cost (49%)
Gold orbStage 2–3≈ 14 Gold15 Gold (20%)
Gold orbfrom stage 4≈ 18 Gold13 Gold + random 5-cost (21%)
Prismatic orbfrom stage 3≈ 40 GoldItem remover + 2 artifact anvils (15%)

The value is a guideline in gold. Champions, anvils and items count with their rough gold value.

What is inside each orb

  • Gray orb (Stage 1–2): 2 random 1-costs (48%), random 2-cost (47%), 2 gold + reforger (3%) – plus 2 more options
  • Gray orb (from stage 3): random 3-cost (49%), 1 Gold + random 2-cost (46%), 3 gold + reforger (3%) – plus 2 more options
  • Blue orb (Stage 1–3): 2 random 3-costs (33%), 3 Gold + random 3-cost (31%), 3 random 2-costs (31%) – plus 3 more options
  • Blue orb (from stage 4): 4 Gold + random 4-cost (49%), 2 Gold + 2 random 3-costs (47%), 8 gold + reforger (3%) – plus 1 more options
  • Gold orb (Stage 2–3): 15 Gold (20%), Anvil (completed item) (18%), 4 gold + Spatula or Frying Pan + reforger (15%) – plus 6 more options
  • Gold orb (from stage 4): 13 Gold + random 5-cost (21%), 2 Gold + 2 component anvils (21%), 10 Gold + 2 random 4-costs (16%) – plus 5 more options
  • Prismatic orb (from stage 3): Item remover + 2 artifact anvils (15%), Masterwork upgrade + item remover + component anvil (15%), 24 gold + masterwork upgrade (15%) – plus 4 more options

Why the stage matters

Gray, blue and gold orbs change their contents with the stage: gray orbs get more valuable from stage 3, blue and gold ones from stage 4. Then they hold more expensive champions or more gold. A gold orb from stage 4, for example, gives 13 Gold + random 5-cost 21% of the time.

Where orbs come from

Orbs drop in PvE rounds – in stage 1 and then in the last round of every stage – and from some augments and encounters. All players get the same number and quality of orbs, only the contents differ. How many orbs and components drop per stage is in the Loot distribution cheatsheet.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Open orbs before your rolldown

If a PvE round is coming up, wait with your big rolldown until you have opened the orbs. Gold, champions or an anvil from them can change your plan – maybe the gold is then enough for one more level, or you get the missing copy for free.

FAQ

What is a gold orb worth?

About 14 gold, from stage 4 about 18 gold – for example as gold, an anvil, champions or a spatula. Every option is in the table.

What is inside a prismatic orb?

A prismatic orb is worth around 40 gold, usually as anvils, masterwork upgrades or a lot of gold.

What is a gray orb worth?

About 2 gold in stages 1–2 and about 3 gold from stage 3, usually as champions.

Loot distribution in TFT Set 18: components and orbs per stage

The PvE rounds of every stage give loot with a random mix: components and orbs in different colours. The cheatsheet shows every combination per stage with its odds. So you can tell whether your drop was good or bad and how many components you can still expect. Here we sum up the numbers per stage and explain how the game balances loot across the match.

3components in stage 1 (average)
11–15components per game from component orbs
11.9components up to stage 4 (average)

Loot per stage

StageComponents (average)Most common lootGold or prismatic orb
133 components + 3× Gray orb (35%)0%
22.43 components + 1× Gray orb (20%)5%
33.54 components + 1× Gray orb (20%)6.2%
43.13 components + 2× Gray orb (17.8%)7%

Component orbs look like blue orbs and hold one random component each. Gold and prismatic orbs are rare in the early stages – if one drops, it is a clear advantage.

How the game balances loot

All players get the same number and quality of orbs – only the contents differ. Across the whole game you get at least 11 and at most 15 components from component orbs. On average it is about 11.9 up to stage 4.

If you got fewer than three components in stage 1, you are among the 18% of games with a weaker start – those rows give more orbs instead, and the floor of 11 components is still guaranteed.

What this means for your items

A completed item needs two components. With around 3 components from stage 1 you can usually build one item and have one left over. By stage 4 an average of 11.9 components come together – enough for about 5 completed items, not counting carousels, anvils and augments.

Build the items for the champion carrying your board early first – usually a tank or an early carry. Save spare components for the carry of your final comp.

From stage 5 on

From stage 5 on there are no random components anymore. In the PvE fight you get a gray orb when the enemy drops to 66% health, a blue one at 33% and an anvil for a completed item when you win.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Plan items around your loot

Expect about 3 components from stage 1 and build the items for your early carry or tank from them. Which component is most likely to come next is shown by the item drop odds.

FAQ

How many components does stage 1 give?

3 components on average, usually exactly three, plus gray or blue orbs.

How many components do you get per game?

At least 11 and at most 15 components from component orbs.

What drops from stage 5 on?

No more random components: a gray orb at 66% of the enemy's health, a blue one at 33% and an anvil for a completed item when you win.

Gold Subscription in TFT Set 18: how much gold do you get?

With the Gold Subscription encounter all players get extra gold at the start of every stage. How much is rolled at the start of the game: one of 5 rows applies for the whole match. On average it is about 48 extra gold from stage 2 to 7. Here you see what each row gives in total and how to use the gold best.

48extra gold on average
216gold in the best row (2%)
35%odds of the most common row

How Gold Subscription works

At the start of the game one row is rolled. It sets how much gold you get at the start of every stage – and it is the same for every player in the lobby. Most often (35%) the gold goes up by 1 per stage.

What each row gives in total

The rare best row brings 216 gold – almost as much as an extra level and a rolldown combined. The weakest row only gives 12 gold.

How to play with Gold Subscription

Since every player gets the same gold, the whole lobby has more gold to spend. Players level earlier and roll more often – strong units get contested faster. You get your edge through interest: reach 50 gold earlier and you earn the maximum every round.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Don't spend the gold right away

The extra gold arrives at the start of every stage. Put it towards your interest first instead of rolling it away – with around 48 extra gold you hit the 50-gold mark much earlier and have more left for level 8.

FAQ

How much gold does Gold Subscription give in total?

From stage 2 to 7 about 48 gold on average. The rare best row (2%) gives 216 gold.

Do all players get the same gold?

Yes, the rolled row applies to every player in the lobby.

When is the gold amount decided?

At the start of the game. The rolled row then applies to every stage.

Reroll Subscription in TFT Set 18: every free reroll

Reroll Subscription gives you free shop rerolls at the start of every stage: 4 in stage 2, then one more each stage up to 9 in stage 7. That is 39 rerolls in total – worth 78 gold. Here you see how the rerolls spread across the game and which comps benefit most.

39free rerolls in total
78gold you save
4rerolls at the start of stage 2

Rerolls per stage

A reroll normally costs 2 gold. The free rerolls arrive at the start of each stage – the later the game, the more you get.

Which comps benefit

Reroll comps that want to bring 1-, 2- or 3-costs to 3 stars benefit most: every free reroll is another shop on your target level without shrinking your interest. But comps looking for 4- and 5-costs on level 8 or 9 also save a lot of gold with the late rerolls.

Compared to Gold Subscription

Gold Subscription gives about 48 gold on average that you can spend freely – on XP, rerolls or interest. Reroll Subscription is worth 78 gold, but only as rerolls. For reroll comps that is no drawback, for fast-8 comps XP matters too.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Use the free rerolls with purpose

Use the free rerolls at the start of each stage to find pairs for 2-star champions instead of spending gold on it. Your gold stays put for interest and the big rolldown – and in reroll comps the same amount of gold gets you to your 3-star units much more often.

FAQ

How many rerolls does Reroll Subscription give in total?

39 free rerolls from stage 2 to 7, saving 78 gold.

Does Reroll Subscription fit reroll comps?

Yes, the free rerolls make hunting for 3-star champions cheaper. The rolldown calculator shows how much gold you need for your goal.

Which champion brings Reroll Subscription?

Reroll Subscription is Kayle's encounter.
