Building emblems in TFT Set 18: every recipe

You build emblems from a spatula or a frying pan plus a second component. Which trait the emblem gives depends on the combination. Set 18 has 8 emblems from the spatula and 8 from the frying pan. The cheatsheet shows every recipe at a glance – here you learn where to get the ingredients and which champion an emblem belongs on.

8emblems from the spatula
8emblems from the frying pan
3tactician items from the two

How to build an emblem

Combine a spatula or a frying pan with another component. You give the finished emblem to a champion – it then also counts for that trait. That way you reach higher trait breakpoints without fielding another champion.

Emblems from the spatula

Blackthorn Emblem, Blossom Emblem, Elderwood Emblem, Fae Emblem, Inferno Emblem, Lunar Emblem, Primal Emblem and Sprykin Emblem.

Emblems from the frying pan

Brawler Emblem, Executioner Emblem, Hunter Emblem, Invoker Emblem, Rapidfire Emblem, Ravager Emblem, Spellweaver Emblem and Vanguard Emblem.

Tactician items

Combine spatulas and frying pans with each other and you get tactician items instead of emblems:

  • Tactician's Cape: Spatula + Frying Pan
  • Tacticians Crown: Spatula + Spatula
  • Tacticians Shield: Frying Pan + Frying Pan

Emblems you cannot build

Coven Emblem, Defender Emblem, Flora Fatalis Emblem and Juggernaut Emblem – these emblems have no recipe. You only get them in other ways, for example through augments or encounters.

Where to get a spatula

  • Gold orbs: in stages 2–3 a gold orb holds a spatula or frying pan 15% of the time.
  • Carousel: some carousels offer spatulas.
  • Augments: some augments give spatulas, frying pans or emblems directly – for example Call to Chaos.
  • Encounter: with Emblem Ensemble (2.3% of games) you start with 3 random emblems.
Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Put the emblem on the right champion

An emblem pays off most on a champion that does not have the trait yet and stays in your team until the end – ideally a tank or carry you will not sell anymore. With two emblems even the prismatic breakpoints of some traits come within reach.

FAQ

How do you build an emblem in TFT?

Combine a spatula or a frying pan with a component. The table shows which emblem you get.

What is the difference between spatula and frying pan?

Both build emblems, but for different traits: the spatula makes 8 emblems, the frying pan 8.

Where do you get a spatula?

For example from gold orbs, the carousel or augments and encounters that give spatulas or emblems.

Winning stage 1 solo in TFT Set 18

In stage 1 you fight PvE enemies. Some 1-cost champions win these rounds on their own, wherever they stand. That way you do not need to spend extra gold on the early rounds and can start earning interest sooner. Here you see which champions can do it this set and how to use the advantage.

Which champions win alone

  • Round 1-3: Akali (Inferno, Adaptor and Ravager), Camille (Coven and Ravager), Rek'Sai (Blackthorn and Brawler) and Yorick (Blossom, Juggernaut and Summoner)
  • Round 1-4: Camille (Coven and Ravager)

The position on the board does not matter – the champion wins the round from any hex.

How to use the advantage

In stage 1 only buy what you need for your start anyway. If you have one of the champions above, it is enough for the PvE rounds – you carry the saved gold into stage 2. There every full 10 gold earns interest each round, and you can level earlier or roll with purpose.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Don't buy everything

Many players buy every champion in stage 1 to win the PvE rounds safely. With the champions from this cheatsheet that is not necessary – keep the gold and start stage 2 with a lead.

FAQ

Which 1-cost wins stage 1 alone?

Round 1-3: Akali, Camille, Rek'Sai and Yorick. Round 1-4: Camille.

Why win stage 1 alone?

You win the PvE rounds without extra buys and keep your gold for interest or an early level.

Does the position matter?

No, the champions from the table win the round from any hex.

Trait Ladder in TFT Set 18

Trait Ladder is a stage 2 augment. You get a random emblem right away. After that it rewards you every time you field enough active traits in a PvP round – starting at 2. After each reward the required number goes up by one and the reward gets bigger, up to 14 traits.

Which traits count

Only non-unique traits count – traits that belong to a single champion do not move you up the ladder. In Set 18, 0 traits are already active with 2 champions. They get you up the ladder fastest.

Every reward

  • 2 traits: Reforger
  • 3 traits: gold
  • 4 traits: gold
  • 5 traits: component
  • 6 traits: gold (50%) or 3-costs (50%)
  • 7 traits: component anvil
  • 8 traits: components (57%) or full item anvil (43%)
  • 9 traits: 5-costs
  • 10 traits: gold
  • 11 traits: Tactician's item
  • 12 traits: 4-costs + Lucky Chest
  • 13 traits: components
  • 14 traits: Masterwork Upgrade

Which boards it fits

It fits best with flexible boards that activate many small trait breakpoints at once instead of pushing a single trait. The emblem from the start helps you open another trait. Plan your board in the team builder to see how many traits your units reach.

How often you are offered Trait Ladder

Trait Ladder is a prismatic augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is prismatic – which is the case in 9.2% of games. Even then it is just one of many prismatic augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

Which traits count for Trait Ladder?

Every active trait that is not unique. Traits of a single champion do not count.

What is the top reward of Trait Ladder?

At 14 active traits: Masterwork Upgrade plus gold.

We Stick Together in TFT Set 18

We Stick Together (stage 2) gives you an emblem of a random trait and an anvil for a completed item. All your champions with that trait gain 30% attack speed. Which trait you get is random – the cheatsheet shows the 13 traits that can come up in Set 18.

The possible traits

Blackthorn, Blossom, Coven, Elderwood, Executioner, Fae, Hunter, Inferno, Invoker, Rapidfire, Ravager, Spellweaver and Sprykin.

Traits not on the list cannot come from this augment – even if they have an emblem.

How to get the most out of it

The attack speed applies to every champion with the trait. The more of them you field, the stronger the augment – especially if your carry is one of them. Give the emblem to a champion that does not have the trait yet, so it also gets the 30%. The item anvil makes your board stronger right away.

How often you are offered We Stick Together

We Stick Together is a prismatic augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is prismatic – which is the case in 9.2% of games. Even then it is just one of many prismatic augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

Which traits work with We Stick Together?

Blackthorn, Blossom, Coven, Elderwood, Executioner, Fae, Hunter, Inferno, Invoker, Rapidfire, Ravager, Spellweaver and Sprykin.

What does We Stick Together give?

An emblem of a random trait, a completed item anvil and 30% attack speed for every champion with that trait.

When can you get We Stick Together?

As an augment on stage 2.

Loaded Dice in TFT Set 18

Loaded Dice (stage 2) makes your luck predictable: dice and coins give you better results. Right away you roll a die and get gold equal to the number, then you flip a coin. With Loaded Dice the die is guaranteed to show a 6 and the coin is guaranteed to land heads. The cheatsheet lists every augment that benefits.

Which augments benefit

  • Coin Flip (Stage 2): guaranteed heads
  • Feeling Lucky (Stage 3): guaranteed heads
  • A Magic Roll (Stage 3): guaranteed 14+ dice total
  • Flip Frenzy (Stage 3/4): first 5 flips guaranteed heads
  • Die Roll (Stage 3/4): guaranteed 6
  • Golden Gamble (Stage 3/4): guaranteed heads (Radiant Lucky Item Chest)

When it pays off

On its own Loaded Dice is a small augment. It gets strong when gamble augments like A Magic Roll or Die Roll are offered later: then you get the best reward instead of a random result. So take it mainly when you want to go for a luck strategy.

How often you are offered Loaded Dice

Loaded Dice is a silver augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is silver – which is the case in 25.7% of games. Even then it is just one of many silver augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

What does Loaded Dice do?

Dice rolls are guaranteed to show a 6, coin flips are guaranteed heads.

Which augments does Loaded Dice work with?

Coin Flip, Feeling Lucky, A Magic Roll, Flip Frenzy, Die Roll and Golden Gamble.

Blossom's Call in TFT Set 18

Blossom's Call (stage 4) ties Blossom's wisps to new champions: when you buy a wisp, you also get a random Blossom champion whose cost matches the wisp. You also get a Yunara, a Yorick and a Karma right away. The cheatsheet shows per stage which costs are possible at which wisp price.

These champions are possible

Every Blossom champion in Set 18: Karma (1 Gold), Yorick (1 Gold), Yunara (2 Gold), Master Yi (3 Gold), Ahri (4 Gold), Sett (4 Gold) and Ashe (5 Gold).

Wisp price and cost

  • Stage 4: 0 gold → 1-cost · 1–2 gold → 1/2/3-cost · 3 gold → 2/3-cost · 4 gold → 2/3/4-cost · 5–7 gold → 3/4-cost · 8+ gold → 3/4/5-cost
  • Stage 5: 0–1 gold → 1/2/3/4-cost · 2–3 gold → 2/3/4-cost · 4 gold → 3/4-cost · 5+ gold → 3/4/5-cost
  • Stage 6: 0–1 gold → 2/3/4/5-cost · 2–10 gold → 3/4/5-cost · 11+ gold → 5-cost

The more gold a wisp costs, the more expensive the champion. 5-costs only show up with expensive wisps or in late stages.

How often you are offered Blossom's Call

Blossom's Call is a gold augment for 4-2. It can only be offered when that augment round is gold – which is the case in 67.9% of games. Even then it is just one of many gold augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

For Blossom boards

The augment pays off most when you already play Blossom and buy wisps. Every wisp then brings an extra champion – so you reach higher Blossom breakpoints faster.

FAQ

Which champions does Blossom's Call give?

Only Blossom champions, matching the cost of the bought wisp – plus Yunara, Yorick and Karma right away.

When does Blossom's Call give 5-cost champions?

They are possible on stage 4 from 8 gold, on stage 5 from 5 gold and always on stage 6.

Expedition in TFT Set 18

Expedition is a stage 2 augment. You get a 3-cost champion right away. After that you lose the champion on the rightmost bench slot at the start of every round. Once you have lost champions worth 33 gold this way, you get a big reward.

The two rewards

  • gold + 5-costs
  • component anvil + Masterwork Upgrade

The cheatsheet shows both options.

How to play Expedition

Put champions you no longer need on the rightmost bench slot on purpose – the more expensive, the faster you reach 33 gold. Keep the slot clear when an important champion is there. That way you fill the bar without weakening your board.

How often you are offered Expedition

Expedition is a silver augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is silver – which is the case in 25.7% of games. Even then it is just one of many silver augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

What does Expedition give?

A 3-cost champion right away. After losing champions worth 33 gold: 15 gold and two 5-cost champions, or a component anvil and a masterwork upgrade.

Which champion do you lose with Expedition?

At the start of every round, the champion on the rightmost bench slot.

Booster Pack in TFT Set 18

Booster Pack gives you a pack of random champions. There are three tiers – Booster Pack, Booster Pack+ and Booster Pack++ – the higher, the more gold is in the pack and the more expensive the guaranteed champion. The cheatsheet shows every possible pack with its odds.

The three packs

AugmentChampions worthguaranteed at leastPacks
Booster Pack12 Goldone 3-cost10
Booster Pack+18 Goldone 4-cost11
Booster Pack++26 Goldone 5-cost12

Some champions in the packs already come at 2 or 3 stars. That counts towards the value.

When it pays off

Booster packs give you a lot of gold in champions at once – good for fielding a strong board early or finding pairs for 2 stars. The basic pack only holds a 4-cost 1.5% of the time, while Booster Pack++ always contains at least one 5-cost. Selling champions you don't need turns part of it back into gold.

FAQ

What are the odds of a 4-cost in Booster Pack?

1.5% – only one of the packs contains a 4-cost.

Does Booster Pack++ always give a 5-cost?

Yes, every possible pack contains at least one 5-cost champion.

Frontline Foundation in TFT Set 18

Frontline Foundation (stage 2) gives you a 1-cost tank that already has 2 stars, plus an emblem of its class. Your frontline stands early, and the emblem opens another trait. The cheatsheet shows which champions are possible and which emblem comes with each.

Possible champions

  • Kobuko ★★ + Brawler emblem
  • Leona ★★ + Defender emblem
  • Yorick ★★ + Juggernaut emblem
  • Rek'Sai ★★ + Brawler emblem
  • Ornn ★★ + Defender emblem
  • Rakan ★★ + Vanguard emblem

How to use it

A 2-star tank is a solid frontline in stage 2. In the long run the emblem often matters more: give it to a champion that stays until the end, so it does not get sold with the early tank.

How often you are offered Frontline Foundation

Frontline Foundation is a gold augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is gold – which is the case in 65.1% of games. Even then it is just one of many gold augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

Which champions does Frontline Foundation give?

Kobuko, Leona, Yorick, Rek'Sai, Ornn and Rakan – each at 2 stars with the emblem of its class.

Backline Blueprint in TFT Set 18

Backline Blueprint (stage 2) gives you a 3-cost champion that is not a tank, plus an emblem of its class. It is the counterpart to Frontline Foundation: instead of an early frontline you get a champion for the back row.

Possible champions

  • Azir + Executioner emblem
  • Cassiopeia + Spellweaver emblem
  • Diana + Ravager emblem
  • Mama Beak + Rapidfire emblem
  • Tristana + Hunter emblem

How to use it

If the champion fits your comp, you have an early carry or a copy towards 2 stars. If not, the emblem is the real prize – it opens a trait you could not reach otherwise.

How often you are offered Backline Blueprint

Backline Blueprint is a gold augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is gold – which is the case in 65.1% of games. Even then it is just one of many gold augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

Which champions does Backline Blueprint give?

Azir, Cassiopeia, Diana, Mama Beak and Tristana – each with the emblem of its class.

Warpath in TFT Set 18

Warpath is a stage 2 augment. You get a 2-star 2-cost champion right away. Once you have dealt 80 damage to players, a chest with expensive champions and items opens.

What is inside the chest

  • three 5-cost champions
  • a 2-star 4-cost champion
  • two completed item anvils

How to play Warpath

You only deal damage when you win fights – and the more of your units survive, the more. So Warpath fits strong early boards that play for a win streak. If you lose, you wait a long time for the chest.

How often you are offered Warpath

Warpath is a gold augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is gold – which is the case in 65.1% of games. Even then it is just one of many gold augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

What does Warpath give?

A 2-star 2-cost right away. After 80 player damage: three 5-cost champions, a 2-star 4-cost and two full item anvils.

How fast does the Warpath chest open?

As soon as you have dealt 80 damage to players in total – a win streak makes it much faster.

Slightly Magic Roll in TFT Set 18

Slightly Magic Roll (stage 2) rolls one six-sided die. Every number gives a different reward – each with a 1 in 6 chance. The cheatsheet shows all six results.

All six results

  • 1: free rerolls
  • 2: gold
  • 3: 2-cost ★★ + gold
  • 4: full item + Reforger
  • 5: +160 HP board-wide
  • 6: random emblem

Is the roll worth it?

The results range from free rerolls to a random emblem. No result is bad, but you cannot plan what you get. With Loaded Dice the die is guaranteed to show a 6.

How often you are offered Slightly Magic Roll

Slightly Magic Roll is a silver augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is silver – which is the case in 25.7% of games. Even then it is just one of many silver augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

What does Slightly Magic Roll give for each number?

1: free rerolls · 2: gold · 3: 2-cost ★★ + gold · 4: full item + Reforger · 5: +160 HP board-wide · 6: random emblem

How do you get a guaranteed 6?

With the Loaded Dice augment.

Call to Chaos in TFT Set 18

Call to Chaos is a stage 4 gamble augment: you get one of 9 powerful rewards, each with about 11%. They range from a lot of gold, XP and rerolls to anvils, lucky chests and a golden egg.

Every reward

  • gold – 58 Gold
  • XP – 64 XP
  • shop rerolls – 40 free rerolls
  • full item anvil + Golden Egg – Completed item anvil + Golden Egg
  • Radiant Lucky Item Chest – 8 Gold + Radiant Lucky Item Chest + Item Remover
  • component anvils + Pan + Spat – 2× Component anvil + Frying Pan + Spatula
  • Thief's Gloves – 3× Thief's Gloves + Item Remover
  • Lucky Item Chests – 3× Lucky Item Chest + Item Remover
  • unique components – 6 components

When to take it

Every reward is strong on its own, but they fit different plans: gold and XP help any board, rerolls mainly help reroll comps, anvils and chests help your carry. Take Call to Chaos when your board is flexible enough to make use of any reward.

How often you are offered Call to Chaos

Call to Chaos is a prismatic augment for 4-2. It can only be offered when that augment round is prismatic – which is the case in 26.6% of games. Even then it is just one of many prismatic augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

What can Call to Chaos give?

gold, XP, shop rerolls, full item anvil + Golden Egg, Radiant Lucky Item Chest, component anvils + Pan + Spat, Thief's Gloves, Lucky Item Chests and unique components.

The Golden Egg in TFT Set 18

The Golden Egg (stage 4) gives you a golden egg that hatches after 11 rounds. Every win against a player makes it hatch one round sooner. It holds plenty of loot – from a lot of gold with a Tactician's Crown to completed and radiant items.

What can be inside

  • 15%: 88 Gold + Tacticians Crown
  • 15%: 30 Gold + 2× Tacticians Crown + Thief's Gloves
  • 10%: 10 Gold + Tacticians Crown + Random radiant item + Random artifact + random full item + Item Remover
  • 10%: 25 Gold + Infinity Force + Zhonya's Paradox + The Indomitable + Champion Duplicator + 2× Item Remover
  • 15%: 10 Gold + Tacticians Crown + 2× Random radiant item
  • 15%: 25 Gold + Tacticians Crown + Radiant Thief's Gloves + Thief's Gloves
  • 10%: 30 Gold + Tacticians Crown + 4× 5-cost + 2× Champion Duplicator
  • 10%: 10 Gold + Tacticians Crown + Infinity Edge + Jeweled Gauntlet + Striker's Flail + Hand Of Justice + Quicksilver + Item Remover

How to play the golden egg

Without wins the egg only hatches after 11 rounds – that is a long time. With a win streak it comes much earlier. Plan your board so you survive until it hatches: the loot is huge, but only useful if you still have enough health.

How often you are offered The Golden Egg

The Golden Egg is a prismatic augment for 4-2. It can only be offered when that augment round is prismatic – which is the case in 26.6% of games. Even then it is just one of many prismatic augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

What is inside the golden egg?

One of several rewards, the most common ones with 15% each – for example 88 gold and a Tactician's Crown. Every option is in the table.

When does the golden egg hatch?

After 11 rounds. Every win against a player shortens that by one round.

Missed Connections in TFT Set 18

Missed Connections (stage 3+) gives you one copy of every 1-cost champion. In the game they appear as orbs in a circle on the board. The cheatsheet shows which 14 champions are included and where they lie.

All champions

Akali, Camille, Varus, Veigar, Ornn, Yorick, Xayah, Karma, Pebbles, Rek'Sai, Rakan, Leona, Kobuko and Cinderling.

How to use it

14 champions at once are strongest for 1-cost reroll comps: you get free copies of your carries and reach 3 stars faster. It also fills your board for traits with many 1-costs. Champions you don't need can be sold for gold.

How often you are offered Missed Connections

Missed Connections is a silver augment for 3-2 and 4-2. It can only be offered when one of these augment rounds is silver – which is the case in 37.6% of games. Even then it is just one of many silver augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

Akali, Camille, Varus, Veigar, Ornn, Yorick, Xayah, Karma, Pebbles, Rek'Sai, Rakan, Leona, Kobuko and Cinderling.

Slice of Life in TFT Set 18

Slice of Life (stage 2) gives you a random champion twice per stage, getting more expensive each stage. The effect ends after you have received a 5-cost champion.

When you get which champion

  • 2-1: a random 2-cost
  • 2-5: a random 2-cost
  • 3-1: a random 3-cost
  • 3-5: a random 3-cost
  • 4-1: a random 4-cost
  • 4-5: a random 4-cost
  • 5-1: a random 5-cost

That is 7 champions worth 23 gold in total.

How to use it

The champions are random, but each is worth gold: if one fits, it is a free copy for your board. If none fits, you sell it and still gain gold. The augment gives the most when you take it early and stay in the game for a long time.

How often you are offered Slice of Life

Slice of Life is a silver augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is silver – which is the case in 25.7% of games. Even then it is just one of many silver augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

How many champions does Slice of Life give?

7 champions up to round 5-1.

When does Slice of Life end?

After you have received a 5-cost champion.

Hard Commit in TFT Set 18

Hard Commit (stage 2) commits you to a trait: you get a random emblem. Right away and at the start of every stage you also get a 1-star champion with that trait whose cost matches the stage (at most 5), plus 3 gold.

The possible traits

7 traits can come up: Blossom, Brawler, Elderwood, Hunter, Juggernaut, Spellweaver and Vanguard. The table shows the champions from 2-cost upwards you can get for each trait.

How to play it

The name says it: you commit. The augment pays off if you play the trait until the end – then you get a fitting champion and gold every stage. If you switch comps later, it loses most of its value.

How often you are offered Hard Commit

Hard Commit is a prismatic augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is prismatic – which is the case in 9.2% of games. Even then it is just one of many prismatic augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

FAQ

Which traits can Hard Commit offer?

Blossom, Brawler, Elderwood, Hunter, Juggernaut, Spellweaver and Vanguard.

What does Hard Commit give every stage?

A 1-star champion with your trait whose cost matches the stage, plus 3 gold.

Solo Leveling in TFT Set 18

Solo Leveling (stage 2) bets everything on one champion: for the next 5 fights you can only field one unit. In return it gets strong bonus stats, and you gain 1 XP for every kill. After that you get 2 components.

The bonus stats

  • 50 % Attack Damage
  • 50 % Ability Power
  • 150 % Attack Speed
  • 10 % Crit Chance
  • 30 % Damage Amp
  • 525 Health
  • 20 % Durability
  • 20 % Omnivamp

How to play it

5 fights with a single unit usually means a few losses – expect to lose health. Pick a champion that survives long on its own and deals damage, and give it your best items. Every kill brings XP, and after the 5 fights you have 2 more components for your real board.

How often you are offered Solo Leveling

Solo Leveling is a gold augment for 2-1. It can only be offered when that augment round is gold – which is the case in 65.1% of games. Even then it is just one of many gold augments. How likely each tier is in your game is shown by the augment odds.

50 % Attack Damage, 50 % Ability Power, 150 % Attack Speed, 10 % Crit Chance, 30 % Damage Amp, 525 Health, 20 % Durability and 20 % Omnivamp.

How long does Solo Leveling last?

5 fights. After that your team size is back to normal and you get 2 components.

Prismatic traits in TFT Set 18

Field enough champions of a trait and it turns prismatic, with stronger effects than its normal top breakpoint. In Set 18 that works for Blossom and Elderwood. The cheatsheet shows the requirements and what changes.

Prismatic Blossom

Field 11 Blossom (requires at least 2 emblems). Wisps overflow with power, upgrading to their prismatic effects.

Prismatic Elderwood

Field 11 Elderwood (requires at least 2 emblems). Plants star up to 3-star and Deepwood Protectors spawn every 7 seconds.

How to reach the prismatic breakpoint

Your board alone usually cannot hold 11 champions of one trait – you need at least two emblems. Spatulas and frying pans are the key. Where to get them and which emblem comes from which recipe is in the emblem cheatsheet.

FAQ

How does Blossom turn prismatic?

Field 11 Blossom (requires at least 2 emblems). Wisps overflow with power, upgrading to their prismatic effects.

How does Elderwood turn prismatic?

Field 11 Elderwood (requires at least 2 emblems). Plants star up to 3-star and Deepwood Protectors spawn every 7 seconds.

Coven loot in TFT Set 18

Coven gathers Essence when your champions kill enemies – and even more when you lose a PvP round. From 40 Essence you decide: convert it into loot now or keep gathering. Every tier needs more Essence and gives better loot, up to 800 Essence. The cheatsheet shows every tier with all possible rewards.

Essence per breakpoint

Coven championsper killper loss
3222
4228
5335
71060

With more Coven champions you gather much faster – especially through losses.

The loot tiers

  • 40 Essence: 3 possible rewards, for example 4 Gold
  • 85 Essence: 3 possible rewards, for example 2 Gold + 1 component
  • 130 Essence: 3 possible rewards, for example 1 component + 3× Caitlyn or 3× Elise
  • 185 Essence: 4 possible rewards, for example Completed item anvil + 1 component
  • 250 Essence: 5 possible rewards, for example 20 Gold + Completed item anvil + Completed item anvil
  • 365 Essence: 6 possible rewards, for example 27 Gold + Random radiant item + Random radiant item + 2× Item Remover + 2× Reforger
  • 500 Essence: 5 possible rewards, for example 3× Random radiant item + Completed item anvil + Completed item anvil + 3× Item Remover + 3× Reforger
  • 650 Essence: 3 possible rewards, for example 30 Gold + 3× 5-cost + 3× 5-cost + 3× 5-cost + Tacticians Shield + Random radiant item + Random radiant item + Random radiant item + Golden Item Remover
  • 800 Essence: 2 possible rewards, for example 100 Gold + 3× Tactician's Cape + 6× Random radiant item + Golden Item Remover

Convert or keep gathering?

Converting early gives you loot right away for a stronger board. Gathering on risks health – especially since losses bring the most Essence – but can reach one of the big tiers. Keep an eye on your health: a big reward only helps if you can still use it.

FAQ

How much Essence does Coven get per kill?

(3) 2 per kill and 22 per loss, (4) 2 per kill and 28 per loss, (5) 3 per kill and 35 per loss and (7) 10 per kill and 60 per loss.

How much Essence do you need for the best Coven loot?

800 Essence.

Riftbeast shop & buffs in TFT Set 18

With 5 Riftbeasts every third shop is full of Riftbeasts. These shops use preset lineups instead of the normal shop odds – the cheatsheet shows per level how likely at least one copy of each Riftbeast is. It also lists the buff each Riftbeast gets with the Alpha Mark.

The Riftbeast shop

From 5 Riftbeasts, your next shop after every third combat is full of Riftbeasts. Which ones show up depends on your level. On level 8 the most common are Krug (76%), Mama Beak (52%) and Gromp (51%). The Elder Dragon only appears from level 9 (5%), on level 10 with 45%.

The odds cover levels 4 to 10 and count at least one copy in the shop. 3-star Riftbeasts are not taken into account.

The Alpha Mark buffs

(3) Use the Alpha Mark to grant a Riftbeast their unique Buff.

  • Cinderling – Scarlet Buff: Gains 22% Attack Damage each cast.
  • Pebbles – Teal Buff: Gain 2 Mana Regen for every 4 seconds channeled.
  • Gromp – Purple Buff: Every 5 seconds, Gromp gains 30% Ability Power.
  • Murkwolf – Grey Buff: Gain Precision and 25% Crit Chance, increased up to 75% based on missing Health.
  • Scuttlecrab – Green Buff: When allies fall below 50% Health, they restore 15% max Health.
  • Mama Beak – Orange Buff: Dealing physical damage reduces enemy Armor by 2.
  • Krug – Slate Buff: On death, Krug and Kruglettes shield allies for 8% max Health.
  • Brambleback – Red Buff: Attacks 1% Burn enemies and heal Brambleback for 5% max Health.
  • Sentinel – Blue Buff: Each time Sentinel casts, allies gain 2 Mana Regen.
  • Elder Dragon – Elder Dragon Buff: Damaging an enemy below 12% Health executes them.

FAQ

How often is there a Riftbeast shop?

With 5 Riftbeasts, after every third combat.

From which level can the Elder Dragon show up in the Riftbeast shop?

From level 9 (5%), on level 10 with 45%.

Blackthorn bonus stats in TFT Set 18

With Blackthorn, the ally on the Blackthorn hex is sacrificed before combat. All your champions gain health, Blackthorn champions also gain stats based on the sacrifice's role, star level and cost. The cheatsheet shows every value for tanks, AD and AP champions.

What the sacrifice's role gives

  • Tank: 17% max health and 12 armor and magic resist (base value)
  • AD champion: 24% attack damage and 14% attack speed
  • AP champion: 10% damage amp and 2 mana regen

These base values are multiplied by the sacrifice's cost and stars – an expensive sacrifice with many stars gives several times as much.

The Blackthorn breakpoints

Blackthorn is active with 2, 4 and 6 champions. Every higher breakpoint gives more health to everyone and makes the bonuses for your Blackthorn champions stronger.

Whom to sacrifice

Put a champion on the hex that you do not need in combat anyway – for example a copy you will sell later. The role decides which stats your Blackthorn champions get: if they need more durability, sacrifice a tank, if they need more damage, an AD or AP champion. The battle simulator shows each champion's role.

FAQ

Which champion should you sacrifice?

The more expensive and the more stars, the higher the bonuses. The sacrifice's role decides the stats: tanks give health and resists, AD champions attack damage and attack speed, AP champions damage amp and mana regen.

Do all champions get something from the sacrifice?

All champions gain health. Only Blackthorn champions get the extra stats based on role.

Fae pixies & gold in TFT Set 18

Your team's damage, healing and shielding attracts Pixies. Each Pixie grants Fae champions attack damage and ability power and heals them when they fall below 50% health. After 7 Pixies, Golden Pixies come instead and give gold. The cheatsheet shows every threshold and value.

When Pixies arrive

The first Pixie arrives at 2,000 damage, healing and shielding, the 7th at 155,000. The values add up across the game – the harder your board fights, the faster the bar fills.

Golden Pixies

  • from 170,000: 5 gold
  • from 200,000: 8 gold
  • from 300,000: 12 gold
  • from 400,000: 18 gold
  • from 500,000: 25 gold
  • from 600,000: 50 gold
  • from 888,888: 777 gold

The last threshold at 888,888 even gives 777 gold – you only reach it in very long games.

The Embiggen augment

Fae pixies are now larger and grant 50% more Attack Damage and Ability Power. Fae champions gain 18% Attack Damage and Ability Power immediately.

FAQ

How much gold do Golden Pixies give?

From 5 gold at 170,000 up to 777 gold at 888,888.

What does the Embiggen augment do?

Fae pixies are now larger and grant 50% more Attack Damage and Ability Power. Fae champions gain 18% Attack Damage and Ability Power immediately.

Primal blessings in TFT Set 18

Primal lets you pick one of 4 blessings: Turtle, Bear, Tiger and Phoenix. Each blessing boosts your team in a different way – from healing and executes to attack speed and components. The cheatsheet shows what each blessing does.

The blessings at a glance

  • Turtle: Your team heals for 4% of their max Health every 4 seconds.
  • Bear: Primal damage executes enemies below 12% Health.
  • Tiger: After 6 seconds, Primal champions gain 35% Attack Speed and your team gains 15% Attack Speed.
  • Phoenix: Every 15 Primal takedowns, gain a component. Max 4.

Which blessing to pick

Primal is active with 2 and 4 champions. Which blessing is best depends on your board: the healing helps boards that fight long battles, the execute boards with a lot of Primal damage, the attack speed teams with auto-attack carries. The component blessing pays off if you rack up kills early and still need items.

FAQ

What does the Turtle blessing do?

Your team heals for 4% of their max Health every 4 seconds.

What does the Bear blessing do?

Primal damage executes enemies below 12% Health.

What does the Tiger blessing do?

After 6 seconds, Primal champions gain 35% Attack Speed and your team gains 15% Attack Speed.

What does the Phoenix blessing do?

Every 15 Primal takedowns, gain a component. Max 4.

Avatar (Lux) in TFT Set 18

As the Avatar, Lux gains a bonus effect on her ability based on her chosen trait. There are 9 traits to choose from – Blackthorn, Blossom, Coven, Elderwood, Fae, Inferno, Lunar, Primal and Solar. The chosen trait counts twice for trait breakpoints. The cheatsheet shows every effect and Lux's base ability.

Lux's base ability

  • Passive: On cast, all allies that share a trait with Lux gain 3/3/100 mana.
  • Active: Fire a laser towards the most enemies in a line that deals 375/565/6500 magic damage, reduced by 25/25/10% for each enemy hit (minimum 40%).

The effects per trait

  • Blackthorn: Stuns targets hit for 1 second.
  • Blossom: The first target hit is dealt 10% bonus damage.
  • Coven: Reduces the Armor and Magic Resist of targets hit by 8 for the rest of combat.
  • Elderwood: Casts grant all allies 2.5% increased max Health for the rest of combat.
  • Fae: Heals the lowest percent Health ally for 18% of ability damage dealt.
  • Inferno: Restores 8 mana per takedown.
  • Lunar: Applies 10% Vulnerable to enemies hit for 4 seconds.
  • Primal: Gain 50% Attack Speed for 6 seconds after cast.
  • Solar: Deal 15% bonus damage. For each unique 3-star champion fielded, deal an additional 12% damage.

Which trait to pick

First pick the trait your board already plays: since it counts twice, it gets you to a higher trait breakpoint. The bonus effect on Lux comes on top. If you have an Avatar on your bench or board, every further Avatar in the shop takes on the same trait.

FAQ

What does Lux do as the Avatar?

Active: Fire a laser towards the most enemies in a line that deals 375/565/6500 magic damage, reduced by 25/25/10% for each enemy hit (minimum 40%).

Which trait is strongest for Lux?

It depends on your team: the trait you already play gives Lux its effect and counts twice for your trait breakpoints.

Cheatsheet
Sprykin 3 / 5 / 7

You get a Best Furry Friend (BFF). Put a Sprykin on it to choose its Rider. Small Furry Friend (Stage 2+) adds a second summon (SFF) that is 45% as powerful.

BFF vs SFF effects
BFF
  • (3) Rider: 15 % · 15 %

  • (7) Rider: 55 % · 55 % · 100% of the BFF's ability applies to your Sprykin champions
SFF
  • (3) Rider: 6,75 % · 6,75 %
  • (5) Rider: 18 % · 15,75 % · 50% of the BFF's ability applies to your Sprykin champions
  • (7) Rider: 24,75 % · 24,75 % · 100% of the BFF's ability applies to your Sprykin champions
BFF ability (melee)
BFF

The BFF roars, healing the Rider and other allies for a % of their max Health.

  • (3) 10 % Rider
  • (5) 13 % Rider, 6,5 % other allies
  • (7) 16 % Rider, 16 % other allies

Sprykin BFF & SFF in TFT Set 18

Sprykin gives you a Best Furry Friend (BFF). Put a Sprykin champion on it and it becomes the rider. The Small Furry Friend augment adds a second, smaller friend (SFF) from stage 2 with 45% of the strength. The cheatsheet shows the values for melee and ranged riders.

The Sprykin breakpoints

Sprykin is active with 3, 5 and 7 champions. At every breakpoint the rider gains more health and attack speed. From the second breakpoint on, your Sprykin champions also get part of the BFF's ability.

Melee or ranged?

Which stats the BFF gives depends on whether the rider fights in melee or at range. Ranged riders get the higher percentages in the table, melee riders stand in front and take more hits instead. Put the champion on the BFF that your board is missing right now.

The Small Furry Friend augment

As long as Sprykin is active, you get a second BFF summon at 45% strength, plus a Teemo, a Veigar and a Kobuko. It pays off if you play Sprykin until the end.

FAQ

How strong is the Small Furry Friend?

It is 45% as strong as the BFF.

How do you choose the BFF's rider?

Put a Sprykin champion on the BFF – it then becomes the rider.

Patch schedule for TFT Set 18: every date

Riot ships TFT patches about every two weeks. The patch schedule lists every date of Set 18 with its events, from the battle pass to tournaments. The table marks the current and the next patch automatically. Next up is patch 18.6 on November 4, 2026.

How often TFT gets patched

In Set 18 there are 14 days between two patches on average. In between there are sometimes B-patches like 18.6B – small fixes when something is too strong or broken. Every patch can change the strength of champions, items and augments.

Upcoming dates

  • Patch 18.6 – November 4, 2026: 1 week patch, 4v4 Superbrawl
  • Patch 18.6B – November 11, 2026: Worlds, Set 19 PBE
  • Patch 19.1 – December 1, 2026: Set 19 launches

When Set 19 launches

Set 19 launches with patch 19.1 on December 1, 2026. From patch 18.6B (November 11, 2026) you can already try it on the PBE. Until then Set 18 stays live.

Events this set

Battle Pass Part 1, TPC Cup #1, Tactician's Trials #1 wk 1, TPC Cup #2, Tactician's Trials #1 wk 2, TPC Cup #3, Battle Pass Part 2, Tactician's Trials #2, Regionals, 1 week patch, 4v4 Superbrawl, Worlds, Set 19 PBE and Set 19 launches.

Pro tipClaudio „CrazYSlayt“

Re-evaluate after every patch

After a patch, comps that were strong before can be much weaker – and the other way round. Read the patch notes and check the tier list before you keep playing your favourite comp.

FAQ

When is the next TFT patch?

Patch 18.6 is planned for November 4, 2026.

When does Set 19 launch?

With patch 19.1 on December 1, 2026.

What is a B-patch?

A small follow-up patch after a main patch that Riot uses to quickly fix bugs or tone down things that are too strong.
